📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, AI-powered workspaces are tech companies’ latest focus, as the industry still struggles to perfect adoption. Microsoft has just put its offering into the ring.

During the keynote for the organization’s Ignite conference on Tuesday, CEO Satya Nadella unveiled Copilot Workspaces, a collaborative, “multiplayer” surface for Copilot’s agentic capabilities.

Also: Microsoft says its latest AI coding model rivals Claude Opus 5.5 at 5% of the cost.

The product, available in Frontier for now, is similar to OpenAI’s ChatGPT Space and several new Anthropic features, including Whiteboard and Sheets, which essentially merge the work tools you’re used to using with an agentic framework.

According to recent reports, “As the evolution of Copilot Notebooks, it’s where people and agents build on each other’s work,” Microsoft said. “An agent drafts a section of a document, and you review. You leave a comment, and an agent picks it up.”.

Microsoft also announced Autopilot, a sort of counterpoint agent to Copilot that “can watch Teams channels, follow up on emails, run recurring work, and manage a project — without waiting for a prompt,” as Microsoft described.

In a demo video during the keynote, the agent appeared to function similarly to OpenAI’s Dots, but for work — employees can tag their Autopilot “like a colleague,” Microsoft stated, and assign it tasks.

Also: 4 ways Anthropic’s fresh Claude Sheets beat using a Google Sheets connector.

Microsoft mentioned the agent will be able to autonomously handle “meetings and follow-ups on its own,” though that claim may be best verified by teams themselves.

Speaking of trust, however, Microsoft noted that “Autopilot runs on the identity, security, and compliance foundation IT already uses,” and that “each Autopilot has its own Microsoft Entra Agent ID and a named manager,” meaning IT can block it as needed.

Industry observers note that “Its sign-ins and actions are logged under its own name, so security teams have a clear audit trail. Powered by Work IQ, it understands how your organization works within existing permissions,” Microsoft stated.

The firm added that employees will soon “be able to bring their personal Autopilot into Workspaces” as well. The feature is also available in Frontier.

In a recent development, nadella also declared a few other productivity features, including a “command center” called Today that spans email, calendar, meetings, tasks, and threads in Teams. Currently in private preview in Outlook and the Copilot app, it includes a personalized briefing and a feed of priorities that updates throughout the day.

“The draft is written and ready for you to edit; the schedule change is already proposed; and the forgotten follow-up is waiting for you to send it, complete with context so you can catch up quickly,” Microsoft mentioned of the feature, which sounds like an agentic briefing-cum-morning-assistant.

Also: Nearly 70% of workers use AI regularly now – but many get no time to upskill.

According to recent reports, microsoft also confirmed that Home, now generally available, unifies Chat and Cowork into a singular starting point. That’s similar to Anthropic’s recent consolidation of its chat and agentic Cowork offerings, demonstrating an overall trend toward simplification in workplace AI.

While more companies are finally starting to see a return on their AI investment, agents are still expensive and can promptly rack up costs when unsupervised.

Microsoft unveiled a few tools to track this at Ignite: Agent 365 Business Analytics and Agent 365 Cost Management.

Also: Microsoft wants to put a dollar value on AI’s work – but can you trust the math?

Agent 365, which Microsoft confirmed last year, is the company’s observability platform. Microsoft said Business Analytics, in Frontier Public today, provides insights on what a company is spending on AI and why, and where it’s paying off, as well as forecasts future costs. In a demo during the keynote, Microsoft indicated how admins can see when specific agents’ costs have spiked recently and what (human) employee to notify as a result.

“It starts with a new way to measure your investment: in work completed, not simply tokens,” Microsoft mentioned. “It analyzes the tasks, how long that work typically takes a person, and the share Cowork performed, providing a sophisticated view of the hours your intelligence supports and what the work is worth.”.

Cost Management lets IT see where teams are using AI down to the model.

“Leaders can set spending policies, limits, and proactive alerts and control which models are available,” Microsoft said. Anthropic released a similar tool last month, though it was focused more on making seats as efficient as possible on Teams and Enterprise plans.

#39521. Polaroid’s Portable Printer Got Me Right Back Into Journaling

Polaroid’s Portable Printer Got Me Right Back Into Journaling

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (892 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cnet

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It helped me survive hormonal changes, the usual teen dramas, plus a hefty dose of existential angst.
  • Recent findings suggest that I made multiple attempts to return to journaling throughout the years, with varying success.
  • Recently, however, I found a way for me to actually stick to the habit: a $110 Polaroid Hi-Print pocket printer.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

I loved journaling as a child. It helped me survive hormonal changes, the usual teen dramas, plus a hefty dose of existential angst. Then college called, and I moved to a different country, leaving behind my childhood, my Nirvana cassettes (I’m old, OK?) and, sadly, my journaling habit.

Recent findings suggest that I made multiple attempts to return to journaling throughout the years, with varying success. I’ve delved into bullet journals under the pretense of improving my productivity, but I gave up when it became too much effort. I’ve invested in multiple notebooks and planners, only to eventually neglect them.

Recently, however, I found a way for me to actually stick to the habit: a $110 Polaroid Hi-Print pocket printer.

Industry observers note that it all began when I discovered the wondrous world of journaling TikTok. In short-form videos, creators would show off beautiful journal pages decorated with colored markers, stickers, washi tape and, yes, photos — specifically photos from portable printers because the prints are small enough to fit within the confines of a typical journal or planner. I really liked the idea of decking out my journal pages with photos of my everyday life. I knew I had to get one.

According to recent reports, after a bit of research, I decided on a couple of criteria. First, I wanted the printer to be a dye sublimation printer rather than a ZINK (Zero Ink) printer. Dye sublimation printers essentially use heat to transfer dye onto the paper, while ZINK printers use a special paper that activates under heat with no ink required (hence the name). Dye sublimation prints tend to be higher quality because it transfers the dye in layers of cyan, magenta and yellow, followed by a protective coating.

Second, I wanted the photo to be on sticky paper so that I didn’t have to mess around with glue to add these photos to my journal.

I found quite a number of dye sublimation pocket printers on the market, but the one that caught my eye immediately was the Polaroid Hi-Print 2×3 Generation 2 pocket printer. I fell in love with it the moment I saw it. The sleek white design, the Polaroid logo and that curved rainbow accent on the edge really sealed the deal for me. Call me a sucker for style, I guess.

I purchased a Hi-Print 2×3 “starter set,” which includes the printer along with two 2×3 paper cartridges. Each cartridge has 10 photo sheets, and each sheet is made out of sticky back photo paper, which is exactly what I wanted. Both the Gen 2 and the prior Gen 1 are easy to find; the main difference is the newer one uses a USB-C charging port while the original uses the older Micro-USB port.

Getting started with the printer is simple enough: Download the Polaroid Hi-Print app, pair the printer with your phone and you’re ready to go. The app is fairly easy to navigate. I like that it lets you arrange your photos in collages so you’re not limited to just one photo per sheet. You can also decorate your prints with colorful frames or decorations. The printer even offers a mosaic option that lets you print out one big image using multiple sheets.

It has been revealed that since it’s a dye sublimation printer, the Hi-Print prints out photos in stages. It lays down the different colors in multiple passes (yellow in the first pass, magenta in the second pass, and so forth). Because of that, printing does take a while: around 60 seconds per photo.

But I don’t mind the delay, as the resulting photo quality is superb. The colors are vibrant and the overall image is nice and sharp. The contrast could be a little better, but for a little pocket printer, the quality definitely exceeded my expectations.

There are a few downsides, however. The obvious one is that photo cartridges can be pretty expensive. One pack of 20 sheets is around $17, though you can get it for $14 each if you buy the 5-pack. That’s still almost 70 cents per 2×3 print. If you use multiple prints, that can add up pretty swiftly.

Another downside is that it doesn’t have a super long battery life. It only has a 620mAh battery, which Polaroid claims will last up to 20 photo printing sessions. I only ever use this printer at home, so this isn’t a massive deal for me, but I can see this being a potential disappointment if you want to bring this printer on the road. That remarked, if you do want to charge it, it doesn’t take that long. Polaroid says it takes under an hour, and that feels about right based on my experience.

I’ve had this printer for a few months now, and I’m very pleased with it. Since I use the photos primarily with my journal, I also really appreciate how thin the photo sheets are, so they don’t bulk up the pages too much. I truly enjoy printing out my little creations, cutting out my collages and then decorating my journal with them.

I might not have my childhood back nor my Nirvana cassettes, but at least I’ve finally recaptured the joys of journaling — even if it did require a bit of help from a pocket printer.

iOS 27 gives the Messages app a variety of welcome upgrades, including one I’ve found myself using a lot: a Smart Reply feature that’s now personalized to the user’s writing style.

When the first wave of Apple Intelligence features were announced in 2024, one that I immediately thought sounded useful was Smart Reply.

The idea behind Smart Reply is simple. Rather than needing to manually type out replies in Messages and Mail, your iPhone can offer prewritten replies you can choose and send with a couple taps.

Great in theory, but the ‘Smart’ part of Smart Reply struggled to materialize in iOS 18.

According to recent reports, fortunately, with a key Apple Intelligence upgrade in iOS 27, the newly introduced version of the feature finally lives up to its name. Per Apple:.

Smart Reply in Mail and Messages can now draw on a user’s personalized writing style.

In a recent development, before, Smart Reply would look at the context of a conversation to craft its suggestions. But now, it also aims to match your writing style, punctuation, and tone.

In iOS 18, I almost never used Smart Reply. That’s because despite being fine at suggesting replies that technically worked, those suggestions didn’t sound like me at all.

Sources indicate that that’s changed in iOS 27. Smart Reply now consistently impresses me. It no longer offers generic responses that sound like AI wrote them. Instead, its suggestions actually fit with my normal style of communication.

In a recent development, the only drawback is that right now, you’ll only ever see two Smart Reply suggestions. If Apple expanded the feature by letting you scroll horizontally through more options, I suspect I’d use Smart Reply even more.

Sources indicate that have you been using iOS 27’s Smart Reply feature in Messages? Let us know in the comments.

#39517. Everything Is Falling Apart, and AI’s Fingerprints Are All Over It

📅 20 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 11m • 📚 Deep Dive (2230 w)
📖 Baca
AI & Tech ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Cnet ↗ Open Full Page

Everything Is Falling Apart, and AI’s Fingerprints Are All Over It

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 11 min read (2230 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cnet

⏱️ ~11 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • I have struggled to find the time to write this story about why everything keeps breaking because everything keeps breaking.
  • According to recent reports, microsoft Outlook?
  • Sources indicate that something must be behind all of this, you might think—a massive cyberattack campaign, maybe or AI agents running amok across the internet?
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

I have struggled to find the time to write this story about why everything keeps breaking because everything keeps breaking.

According to recent reports, microsoft Outlook? Broken, for a bit. Air traffic control? Had some issues. Bank with Chase? Monday was not great. But even before that, you had issues if you ran a website with PHP, or had a grocery store freezer connected to the internet, or owned crypto. I am almost certainly forgetting some.

Sources indicate that something must be behind all of this, you might think—a massive cyberattack campaign, maybe or AI agents running amok across the internet? But the answer is more complicated than that. All of these challenges, and the ones that will happen after I write this, are probably unconnected, at least in the concrete sense. But they exist in a world where the infrastructure of the internet and the whole human world it undergirds looks increasingly precarious.

In a recent development, adam Meyers, senior vice president of counter adversary operations at cybersecurity company CrowdStrike, called last month “Black October.” This month? “Blacker November.” December probably isn’t looking great.

“This is not getting better, unfortunately,” Meyers told me.

One massive reason for all of this, although not the only one, is artificial intelligence, but maybe not in the ways you expect.

Recent findings suggest that if it’s connected to the internet, it’s at risk. Websites, sure. But also utilities like power plants and water treatment facilities or, for some reason, grocery store freezers.

In the olden days, like six months ago, a hacker taking control would have required a fairly complicated set of skills, honed over a long career, perhaps in the employ of a government or criminal organization.

Recent findings suggest that artificial intelligence, especially models developed and released this year, has changed things. AI has “democratized” hacking, cybersecurity experts told me. Things that used to require the capabilities and focus of a team of people with a clear goal can be done by a 20-something with an AI model and a specially designed program around it. And you don’t have to be a big or valuable target anymore to be worthy of a hacker’s attention.

Recent findings suggest that at the same time, AI has made it easier to find vulnerabilities. These models and agents — essentially AI models that can do things on their own — can comb through websites or code and find problems that might have escaped the notice of humans. And they can do so more cheaply, meaning they can be turned on code that might not otherwise have gotten a close look. So many vulnerabilities are being exposed that it’s been given an appropriately bleak name: the vulnpocalypse.

Even that defensive advantage is a double-edged sword. Before, it might have taken weeks before a newly discovered vulnerability could be exploited. Now it might take days, even hours. If you’re responsible for a website or any of those things connected to the internet that may or may not still be maintained by their creators, you may not be paying attention and know you should update. You may find yourself liable if a breach leads to a leak of customer data. You may not have the know-how to fix it.

Sources indicate that another risk introduced by AI is that the technology, trained on all the lines of code its creators could find, is really good at writing code. Software engineers know this, and companies are now maintaining smaller teams of human engineers using AI to write more and more software. That code might be OK, but it might not be, and there’s a chance no human ever looked at it to be sure.

Sources indicate that when I connected with John Strand over video chat, he was in Germany for a conference, and he was smiling. That wasn’t good. “You need to understand that whenever an offensive security person smiles and gets excited,” he stated, “it’s bad.”.

It has been revealed that as owner and CEO of Black Hills Information Security, Strand’s job is to test systems for weaknesses, to think like an attacker and poke holes in a client’s defenses. He indicates he’d been getting a bit bored with the work after decades of the same techniques until the cyber capabilities of AI models started to explode at the end of 2025. Fresh AI models were great at finding weaknesses in code, and AI agents could do the boring, time-consuming part.

“You’re seeing something that can automate the kind of grinding grunt work of offensive security and bring that to a human operator much faster,” Strand stated.

According to recent reports, things have only accelerated since the summer. AI agents are capable of more autonomy. And attackers have better tools to refine the often blunt instruments of AI models — harnesses. While an AI model can do a lot of things, a harness provides the tools and direction that allow it to do a specific thing more effectively. Think Anthropic’s Claude Code or OpenAI’s Codex, but for hacking. Perhaps the biggest, most notable harness used by hackers is Artex, a significant-enough threat that the FBI issued a warning last week.

In September and October, a hack of major South Korean banks led to the theft of personal information. Meyers says CrowdStrike determined the attacker was likely a 26-year-old in China using Artex. After asking AI how to do the attack, the hacker succeeded, then asked the AI how to sell the stolen data on Telegram.

“Anybody out there can now be a nation-state-level hacker just by using the tool,” Meyers said.

Despite efforts by major AI developers to limit who can access their biggest and most capable models, the hacking and exploit skills attackers need are within the means of models already in the hands of attackers. That includes open-weight models that hackers can run on their own hardware, away from the guardrails and peering eyes of AI companies and government agencies.

“The genie’s out of the bottle, and there’s no putting it back in,” said Gary Barlet, public sector chief technology officer at Illumio, a firm that specializes in ransomware and breach containment.

In a recent development, AI-powered hackers, whether they’re individual vibe-hackers or government-backed cyberwarfare units intent on damaging critical infrastructure, always have an advantage. They just have to be right once, as the saying goes. Defenders have to be right every time.

The good thing is that the defenders are using the same tools as the attackers. And sometimes they have a head start. Programs like Anthropic’s Project Glasswing, OpenAI’s Daybreak and Google’s Fairwind let cybersecurity experts and high-profile targets like banks and healthcare providers have early access to the most capable models from those developers, often with fewer limits on what the models can find. The goal is to get a jump on patching and fixing the easiest and riskiest problems.

In a recent development, it still might not be enough, and Substantial Tech leaders know it. In an October appearance at the Stanford Graduate School of Business, OpenAI CEO Sam Altman said he no longer thought we’d be able to “just patch all the bugs” and that the problem is one that “is still something that we have not, as organizational leaders or countries or individuals, taken seriously.”.

According to recent reports, and defenders may not have much of a lead in patching bugs anyway, Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella stated this week at the New York Times Dealbook Summit. Previously, when patching a critical system, you might have a week to test it before pushing it to production. “Right now the patch needs to go instantly from being available to being patched in production because it’s being exploited in the wild,” Nadella said. “That’s going to create instability.”.

The PHP vulnerability widely reported in October — with an urgent notice from the PHP Foundation for website owners to patch — stemmed from work through Patch the Planet, part of OpenAI’s Daybreak.

According to recent reports, that’s just one high-profile recent disclosure. But there has been an avalanche of them. The National Vulnerability Database has received more than 10,000 instances of common vulnerabilities and exposures so far in November, after more than 17,000 CVEs in October. For comparison, in October 2025, that figure was less than 5,000.

“There’s effectively this big backlog of security issues in the open-source world that hadn’t been discovered until AI was able to just spend tons of time analyzing it and finding these vulnerabilities,” said Matt Wyckhouse, CEO of Finite State, a cybersecurity organization focused on connected devices.

Sources indicate that it goes well beyond open-source software. The connected devices Wyckhouse focuses on include things like refrigerators and smart home gadgets — the kinds of things that probably didn’t have to be connected to the internet, but are. The source code of the firmware and software powering those products has been seen by far fewer eyes than something like PHP, an incredibly common coding language used by much of the internet. The code running these devices may not be on GitHub or floating around the internet, but an AI model might be able to reverse-engineer it and find an exploit. And suddenly an attacker can turn freezers into ovens. If you think ground beef is expensive now, imagine what would happen if a major retailer’s stock of hamburger all spoiled overnight.

“Refrigeration has to work for our society to function, as it turns out,” Wyckhouse mentioned.

Wherever the vulnerability is found, it has to be patched. That’s where the backlog of concerns is really wreaking havoc. Companies that create or just operate software are swamped with vital, critical issues that have to be fixed now because it could only be hours before an attacker can exploit it. It’s why your computer and the software on it have to upgrade so frequently these days.

“It’s daunting the amount of work and the amount of time it’s going to take to clean this whole thing up,” said Ted Miracco, CEO of the mobile security firm Approov.

And patching isn’t perfect. Sometimes it’s not a cyberattack that causes a system to go down but the fix to prevent it. Software updates are believed to be responsible for several of the recent high-profile outages, including Apple’s issues on Tuesday.

Things get even hairier if the code isn’t great to begin with or presents upcoming problems of its own. And with AI writing even more of it, that’s a growing problem.

Industry observers note that in the backdrop of all of this chaos is the fact that software engineering is one of the industries most disrupted by AI. Models trained on miles of code are great at writing something that works — no matter how many holes are in it. And to CEOs eager to cut costs and boost their companies’ stock prices, the temptation is to lay off engineers and have fewer people use AI to do all that coding.

Substantial Tech has been laying off staff by the thousands this year. Microsoft’s October announcement that it was offering buyouts to 60,000 staff became a key talking point just weeks later when the system powering its Outlook email service went dark for a day. Might things break less often if more people were on hand to maintain them?

“I wouldn’t be surprised if companies start to backtrack on that more,” remarked Ryan McCurdy, vice president of marketing at the database security firm Liquibase.

Companies might also have more junior developers writing and releasing code that would have previously gone through senior developers, with AI replacing the productivity, but not the experience, McCurdy claims.

That means the problem isn’t just the vulnerabilities in existing software, but the vulnerabilities being written into new software or patches to existing software by AI. The same technology is causing the problem, providing the solution and complicating that solution.

Industry observers note that the main thing we can do now is just… wait. Wyckhouse told me he thinks the next two years are going to be a period of growing pains as vulnerabilities are found and patched. The end result should be that everything is more stable.

Industry observers note that “I think software is going to be an order of magnitude more secure by the end of the next year or two than it is today for this reason,” he noted. “It will hurt a bit.”.

Whether you’re an ordinary phone user or a major corporation, updating your software has become more important than ever.

According to recent reports, “You’ve got to patch. You go for a flu shot, and you go and have your preventative healthcare,” Meyers noted. “You need to do the same thing when it comes to cybersecurity.”.

But consumers aren’t without power, especially when it comes to data breaches. If a firm isn’t properly maintaining its systems and protecting your privacy or security online, don’t use it. Having your data hacked and compromised has become ordinary. We get letters in the mail saying someone stole data from our bank or doctor’s office, and if we jump through the following hoops, we can get 12 months of identity protection.

Industry observers note that we don’t have to put up with it, Barlet claims. “I think we need to start having higher expectations from the companies we’re consuming from,” he mentioned.

By Neil Patel – Nov 20, 2026 at 4:00PM EST.

10 stocks we like better than Procter & Gamble ›.

Procter & Gamble (PG +0.91%)shares have climbed only 103% in the past 10 years (as of Nov. 13). The company certainly isn't drawing in growth investors, but it can be a top choice for income seekers.

Here's how many shares of this consumer staples stock you would need to generate $1,000 in yearly dividends.

Image source: Procter & Gamble.

According to recent reports, procter & Gamble right now pays a quarterly dividend of $1.0885 per share, which amounts to $4.354 on an annualized basis. This means you would have to own 230 shares to collect $1,000 in yearly passive income. At the current stock price of $169.83, the investment required totals over $39,000.

Sources indicate that at 2.56%, the dividend yield is healthy. That's much higher than what the S&P 500 index (^GSPC -3.70%) offers.

It has been revealed that investors should be blown away by the payout's durability. In April, the board of directors raised the dividend, which marked the 70th straight year that a hike was approved. What’s more, the business has paid dividends in 136 consecutive years, a mind-boggling track record.

NYSE · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

Recent findings suggest that shareholders can sleep well at night knowing that their income stream is safe. During the keynote at its Ignite conference on Tuesday, Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella announced several fresh models from Microsoft AI (MAI), its lab within the tech giant. But new model releases are almost a dime a dozen these days, and accelerating fast — what really stood out was how Microsoft will let its customers access those models.

Also: Microsoft says its new AI coding model rivals Claude Opus 5.5.

It has been revealed that MAI mentioned it would allow its customers to customize its frontier models with their own data and run them securely in Azure through an initiative called Licensed Weights. It’s essentially a selective approach to open-weight AI: more so than proprietary models from OpenAI and Anthropic, but not fully downloadable on Hugging Face like Mistral’s Le Chonk. Interested companies will need to go through their Microsoft account reps to get started.

“You control who can access it. Your data and adaptations stay entirely yours. And we’ll work with you through Frontier Firm to deliver the custom model and embed it in your own products and agents,” Mustafa Suleyman, CEO of MAI, noted during the keynote.

It has been revealed that the approach should stand out to businesses looking for affordable AI that lets them retain control over their IP. Microsoft stated it would only use customers’ information to train its models if they agreed.

“No one wants to pour their IQ into someone else’s model,” Suleyman said during the keynote, a nod to an argument Palantir CEO Alex Karp has made repeatedly.

The dominant, if simplified, narrative in AI has been that proprietary, expensive models boast peak capabilities but aren’t customizable, while open, cheaper models are customizable but less capable. Microsoft’s AI models don’t necessarily compete with OpenAI and Anthropic yet, but the company has legacy sway with countless businesses. By offering a customizable AI option, it could strike a balance among major tech companies.

According to recent reports, western labs, including Thinking Machines and Mistral, are releasing more competitive open-weight models, but Anthropic and OpenAI still have the overwhelming majority of the enterprise AI market. Though Licensed Weights isn’t an open-weight family of models, it does diversify the open-versus-closed debate a bit and differentiate Microsoft’s offering from OpenAI’s and Anthropic’s. It’s also a smart pairing with Microsoft’s goal to balance price and performance, if businesses find it impressive enough.

Also: Microsoft unveiled Copilot Workspaces at Ignite 2026.

“Averaged over four widely used benchmarks that target the everyday enterprise coding tasks we see in GitHub Copilot, MAI Code 2 gives you 98% of the performance of GPT 6.1 Sol at just 40% of the cost, and against Opus 5.5 it’s an incredible 5% of that cost,” Suleyman mentioned of the upcoming coding model the company unveiled at Ignite.

The organization also released its upcoming image editing model, MAI Image 2.7, on Tuesday, which now leads the category on Artificial Analysis while beating Nano Banana Pro and several GPT image models on price and quality. With Licensed Weights, Microsoft has positioned itself for organizations seeking a reliable blend of ROI tools, customization, security controls, and capability.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that motion-based automations are generally straightforward in Apple Home.
  • HomeKit Weekly is a series focused on smart home accessories, automation tips and tricks, and everything to do with Apple’s smart home framework.
  • According to recent reports, A standard motion sensor uses PIR, which only detects movement, and that works fine in many situations.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that motion-based automations are generally straightforward in Apple Home. The only carve-out is lighting, because some rooms are hard to judge by time of day alone. Depending on the windows and placement against the sun, some rooms might need light-based automations earlier in the day than others. The Lafaer 5-in-1 presence sensor fixes that with a light sensor most motion sensors lack, along with mmWave radar.

HomeKit Weekly is a series focused on smart home accessories, automation tips and tricks, and everything to do with Apple’s smart home framework.

According to recent reports, A standard motion sensor uses PIR, which only detects movement, and that works fine in many situations. If you’re still for long periods, you’re invisible, and the automation assumes the room is empty. The Lafaer LWR02 pairs PIR with 2.4 GHz mmWave radar. The PIR-based motion sees you walking in, and the radar sees the minor stuff, like breathing and shifting on the couch, so the room stays “occupied” for as long as you are in it. The two together also reduce false positives from ceiling fans, curtains, and the dog, because the radar and PIR both must agree before the sensor reports motion.

In Apple Home, that highlights up as an occupancy sensor and a motion sensor from the same device.

Recent findings suggest that “Turn on the lights when someone enters” is a common automation I use, but it can be tricky. What if you only want it when it’s not light outside? Doing it based on time of day sometimes works, but what about depending on where the windows are facing, etc.? You might have a room that gets darker an hour earlier than another room. “Turn on the lights when someone enters, and it’s dark in the room” is what the light sensor can handle for you.

In the Home app, that means triggering a sensor for occupancy, then converting the automation into a Shortcut and adding a condition for the light level. It’s a few extra steps, but it does really give you more fine control over how it works.

Presence, motion, light, temperature, and humidity all come from the same device, and each one appears in Apple Home as its own sensor, so you can build automations around whichever ones fit the room.

It’s IPX3-rated, so bathrooms, kitchens, and laundry rooms are fine to use in. Coverage is about 13 feet for presence and 26 for motion across about 120 degrees, which works in a bedroom, office, or bathroom. It’s not going to cover a great room from one corner. The base is a magnetic half sphere, so you can aim it, and it mounts with adhesive or sits on a shelf. I generally like to use the shelf for these types of sensors.

In a recent development, the Lafaer LWR02 is Matter over Thread, so it pairs directly with a HomePod, HomePod mini, or Apple TV 4K with no Lafaer hub or account needed. It runs on two included AAA batteries, is rated for up to two years, and rechargeable AAAs work with it as well. Thread is why a sensor doing this much can last that long on batteries. All sensor data is processed locally, so it only uses a trickle on the batteries.

Lights that turn off while you’re sitting still in the room are the reason a lot of people stop using motion automations in smart homes. The Lafaer LWR02 fixes that with mmWave radar and then lets you have more granular control of light-based automations based on what’s actually in the environment in the room, not just the time of day.

The Lafaer 5-in-1 presence sensor is available on Amazon.

#39512. One Month and a Half-Million-Plus Folds Later, Our Machine Is Still Testing the iPhone Duo

📅 20 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1123 w)
📖 Baca
Gadgets ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Cnet ↗ Open Full Page

One Month and a Half-Million-Plus Folds Later, Our Machine Is Still Testing the iPhone Duo

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1123 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cnet

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that apple’s $1,999 iPhone Duo folding phone came out a month ago.
  • How many times can we fold the iPhone Duo?
  • It has been revealed that I oversee hardware and software testing as director of lab operations in our lab in Louisville, Kentucky.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that apple’s $1,999 iPhone Duo folding phone came out a month ago. Every day since then, 24 hours a day, seven days a week, a dedicated machine inside CNET’s lab has been folding and unfolding it over and over again. For science.

How many times can we fold the iPhone Duo? As of Friday, Nov. 20, we’re up to more than 565,000 folds and the Duo hasn’t broken yet. The hinge has shown signs of potential failure, however. Our technicians, as well as the cameras and sensors that are part of our testing rig, continue to monitor the situation and collect data.

It has been revealed that I oversee hardware and software testing as director of lab operations in our lab in Louisville, Kentucky. My team and I designed and built this proprietary machine to test foldable phones like Apple’s and its Samsung rival, the Galaxy Z Fold 8 (which we’ve also started testing). I’ve worked on the methodology and build of this testing rig for months in anticipation of Apple’s long-rumored foldable iPhone.

We even named our machine to match its purpose: Meet the Fold-a-Phone.

My team of engineers and testing experts has been watching the iPhone Duo open and close, over and over, for the past few weeks to rigorously and systematically monitor the durability of Apple’s hinge and two screens.

After all, repeatedly folding a phone with bare hands can only get you so far in understanding the complex forces at play between the magnetics that snap the screen shut and the all-critical hinge.

According to recent reports, CNET’s Senior Technology Reporter, Abrar Al-Heeti, has done a beautiful job capturing the iPhone Duo’s pros and cons in her smart, thorough review as well as her one-month-later follow-up. Our Fold-a-Phone machine will add a deep data foundation to complement her real-world experience.

Since Apple hasn’t publicly shared claims of the iPhone Duo’s foldable lifespan, CNET’s Fold-a-Phone machine is poised to provide a wealth of valuable data about Apple’s first foldable phone and competing models in the foldable market.

And yes, you’d better believe we will use our treasure trove of in-house data to share status updates and comparisons during our ongoing testing window with the Duo.

Join CNET’s iPhone Duo livestream on YouTube weekdays from 1 p.m. to 5 p.m. ET, where you can follow along live and watch the Fold-a-Phone do its thing to a Duo.

It has been revealed that the importance of this moment is hard to overstate. Apple’s appearance on the foldable smartfold frontier lags Samsung by seven years (the first Galaxy Fold went on sale in the US in September 2019). Motorola and other phone-makers have long experimented with foldable phones in every shape and size, including a trifold accordion foldable phone we first demoed in 2019.

CNET’s mobile experts, including Al-Heeti and Editor at Large Andrew Lanxon, have discussed the legitimizing effect of the iPhone Duo’s existence on the entire foldable phone landscape, which has previously felt like a new-wave fantasy rather than a mainstream riptide.

Sources indicate that in many ways, Apple’s newfound competition with existing foldable phones completes the portfolio. That is precisely why we’re building the Fold-a-Phone now, and why our proprietary machine, methodology and test data will enrich our collective understanding of the capabilities – and yes, limitations – of foldable phones as our true next-generation mobile device.

It has been revealed that most current foldable phones are rated for 200,000 to 500,000 folds. As such, we knew we needed to create a robust and adaptable machine that could accommodate book- and flip-style foldable phones of any size, dimension and hinge orientation. (Note: The Fold-a-Phone was not built for trifold phones, which present a unique element to the engineering challenge.).

Sources indicate that moreover, we wanted to test the phone the way people would actually use it. No one just sits around opening and closing their foldable phone at top speed all day. Rather, you open it naturally, spend a few minutes watching a video, browsing a web page, or using an app, close it, and then put it in your pocket. This may happen dozens of times per day.

Mimicking this usage on the Fold-a-Phone limits undue stress on the phone hinge and avoids generating excess heat compared to a test built for speed.

Recent findings suggest that we determined that a cadence of roughly 4 seconds could sidestep technical hurdles while also being reasonably fast. The foldable phone takes 1 second to open, 1 second to fully open, 1 second to close and 1 second to fully close. This cycle counts as a single completed fold. Then, the cycle repeats until either the hinge or the screen gives out.

In conceptualizing and building the Fold-a-Phone, our team has used standard, off-the-shelf components to simplify the machine’s development. The essential design consists of two armatures, distinctly designed to perform the opening and closing movements with both force and grace.

It has been revealed that an industrial-grade stepper motor drives each armature, with the host software (running on a connected computer) deterministically adjusting the torque to complete each step of the process while also protecting the phone. If any of the several proximity sensors fail to detect the armature in the correct position, the machine stops immediately.

In a recent development, we also monitor the motors’ power usage to track how well the foldable phone opens and closes over time. We have set up cameras to capture images and video of the test from multiple angles, and we will analyze regular status updates from the computer to determine the current status of the phone and the test.

To ensure we never miss a major development, the entire rig is connected to an EcoFlow Delta 3 Plus power station to guard against electricity outages, and all the output data is saved to multiple locations.

Industry observers note that to secure each phone to the machine, we use our CNET Lab Test-winning 3D printer, the Prusa Core One, to 3D-print a custom “sled” that matches each phone’s exact dimensions. We secure the phone to the sled with heavy-duty double-sided tape (yes, it works!) and then screw the sled onto the machine.

Recent findings suggest that there’s always room for improvement. We’re constantly looking for ways to make the machine run more smoothly and quietly without disrupting the folding rhythm.

Apple’s presence is already changing the game and could very well spur innovation in ways we can’t predict today. But until then, our Fold-a-Phone machine will continue to test the iPhone Duo and its competitors, and CNET’s writers will report on how well these individual hinged devices stand up to the challenge – or fold under pressure.

Industry observers note that the case for the higher-end AirPods 5 ($149) supports wireless charging and Find My. You also get one extra hour of battery life. The higher-end model also adds on-stem volume control, so you can adjust the volume just by swiping up or down on one of the earbud stems.

Here’s a full comparison between both AirPods 5 models:.

The key thing about AirPods 5 is their open-ear design, unlike the in-ear design of the AirPods Pro 3 (more on those later). Even with that open-ear design, AirPods 5 offer incredible Active Noise Cancellation capabilities.

If you are shopping for AirPods 5, I do recommend spending the extra $20 to get the higher-end model. The better charging case alone is worth the extra money. With Find My integration and a built-in speaker, you can track your AirPods and play a sound from the case if you lose them.

If the person you’re shopping for doesn’t like in-ear earbuds, AirPods 5 are an excellent choice.

For most people, though, AirPods Pro 3 are probably the better choice ….

Recent findings suggest that airPods Pro 3 are Apple’s most capable earbuds, even with the introduction of AirPods 5 this year. According to recent reports, I still think AirPods Pro 3 are one of the best products in Apple’s lineup today. I wear mine for multiple hours every single day and can’t imagine life without them. It has been revealed that if you know the person you’re shopping for (whether it’s yourself or someone else) likes the in-ear earbud design, I think AirPods Pro 3 are the best option. The price difference between AirPods 5 and AirPods Pro 3 is very small, and you’re getting a much better product.

Finally, we have AirPods Max. These are Apple’s only option for people who want AirPods in an over-ear headphone form factor. Last year, they were pretty hard to recommend since they’d gone five years without a real upgrade.

This year, however, Apple officially introduced AirPods Max 2, bringing modern features to Apple’s high-end headphones. This includes features like Adaptive Audio, Conversation Awareness, Personalized Volume, and more.

In a recent development, airPods Max 2 are a far more compelling option than AirPods Max were at this time last year. They’re still pricey, but I love the aesthetics and find them very comfortable. There’s something about the premium aluminum design with an elegant Digital Crown that really stands out.

If you’re looking to splurge this holiday season, AirPods Max 2 are a great choice. For more realistic budgets, I think AirPods Pro 3 are the best option.

  • Sources indicate that the Gemini AI improvements got a real-world test during Washington state’s Railroad Fire in July 2026, when Watch Duty issued what it calls its first-ever nighttime Critical Alert.
  • It has been revealed that “This is something the tool also has the capability to do if reports of flooding are communicated via radio,” remarked Dave Merritt, co-founder and chief technology officer of Watch Duty.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that on Friday, Google’s Gemini team confirmed the results of a upcoming partnership with the wildfire-tracking app Watch Duty, after Gemini engineers spent six months embedded with Watch Duty’s first responders. The results cut vital new wildfire dispatch translations down to seconds and helped improve radio communications, which can be rough on the front lines of a new fire.

Sources indicate that the Gemini AI improvements got a real-world test during Washington state’s Railroad Fire in July 2026, when Watch Duty issued what it calls its first-ever nighttime Critical Alert. The alert stemmed from a nearly unintelligible, static-filled 911 call that the Gemini tool transcribed in under 30 seconds. That kind of assistance can help Watch Duty send alerts to affected communities more rapidly and enable first responders to upgrade maps more accurately and make better-informed decisions.

It has been revealed that “This is something the tool also has the capability to do if reports of flooding are communicated via radio,” remarked Dave Merritt, co-founder and chief technology officer of Watch Duty. “Across disasters, we hear feedback every day that first responders are using Watch Duty for additional situational awareness, especially for disasters that span multiple counties.”.

Watch Duty reporters are active and retired first responders who can manually monitor up to 20 different feeds, though static and rapid-fire jargon can make them difficult to follow.

Gemini workers used more than 20,000 hours of Watch Duty radio recordings to train the AI tool to recognize firefighting terms that aren’t in the average dictionary or books that AIs are typically trained on.

Google states the tool is not designed to replace human decision-making in life-or-death situations.

“This tool takes on the demanding work of listening, freeing Watch Duty’s volunteers to focus on what matters most: confirming fires and getting warnings to people while they can still act,” mentioned Stephanie Chew, Google project team lead.

The project was completed at no cost thanks to a Google.org fellowship, and the resulting Watch Duty app features are free to use.

From the data collected, Gemini engineers and Watch Duty identified several measures of success.

One metric was the word error rate, which fell by around 15% after the AI model was implemented. Another sign of success was a jump in Watch Duty volunteers’ satisfaction with their radio transcription tools, from around 35% to 92%.

Industry observers note that the Gemini tool continues to analyze approximately 200 hours of radio speech traffic from 400 feeds per day. The tool was made to handle more than 10,000 radio feeds if necessary.

Industry observers note that the integration could pave the way for broader use across public safety. The platform’s built-in scalability could eventually bring similar audio-clearing tools to local fire departments, 911 call centers and Coast Guard operations, where clear communication is critical under pressure.

Sources indicate that brands are also being noticed by AI agents, with 30% of shoppers saying they were first introduced to a latest brand via AI. And most importantly, 1 in 10 (11%) shoppers would avoid a brand if an AI agent told them to.

Here are some of the key findings from the 2026 holiday shopping research.

Retailers that use AI shopping agents are seeing bigger orders and more loyal customers. The survey found that shoppers who use AI agent referrals are twice as likely to make a purchase. In addition, 39% of shoppers have used AI agents on an e-commerce site, and 80% had a positive experience, while 75% felt more loyal to the brand as a result of the AI agent experience.

Recent findings suggest that shoppers who use AI agents spend 8% more than the average buyer and purchase 23% more items per order. Brands that use AI agents are seeing seven times faster sales growth than brands without them.

Industry observers note that 1 in 3 consumers has used an AI agent, including the widely adopted Meta Muse, now used by 12% of all consumers. Grok Bot is also in high demand.

Sources indicate that the survey found that 28% of consumers give their agents multiple tasks per day. The most common use of AI agents is price comparisons, product reviews, and brainstorming for gift items. Brand discovery is a major benefit of AI agent use cases.

In a recent development, agents as advisors are growing, but agents are not buying products yet, with only 19% of personal agent consumers using logic to check out. Only 9% of consumers allow their personal AI agents to have unrestricted access to their financial details, and 36% have set up a separate credit card for their AI agents.

Also: ZDNET’s favorite tech devices for 2026.

It has been revealed that the majority of consumers (73%) are not comfortable giving personal AI agents their payment information, and 49% are not interested in agents making purchases on their behalf. Consumers do not want to share their purchase history or personal data that could potentially lead to unwanted charges. Shoppers will abandon an AI agent after 2-3 mistakes. If an AI agent makes a bad recommendation, 1 in 3 consumers will blame the AI.

Industry observers note that retailers must adopt AI shopping agents in order to compete. Retailers must be able to service and respond to shopper agents. The ability to detect intent, buying signals, sources of dissatisfaction, and other consumer-related buying patterns at machine scale (significantly faster and higher volume than human scale) will require retailers to invest in AI agentic engagement capabilities.

Look, we weren’t all lucky enough to lock in PTO for the release of Grand Theft Auto 6. Not everyone gets to write a review of the most anticipated video game in recent memory, or live blog their first 24 hours roaming around Vice City.

Industry observers note that A lot of folks are still working away, daydreaming about getting back on the sticks and knocking off corner stores as Jason and Lucia right now. Some people are even on work trips or vacations away from their home consoles right now – let’s keep them in our thoughts.

Industry observers note that but even if you find yourself away from home, that doesn’t mean you’re completely locked out of playing GTA 6. Sure, the game may presently be console-locked to the PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X and S, but there are still clever ways to get the game booted up when you’re on the go.

Here’s everything you need to know about the remote play features that you’ll need to take this modern Bonnie and Clyde story on the road.

So long as you have a PS5 or an Xbox with GTA 6 downloaded and ready to go, you can experience the game through smaller devices even when you’re away from home.

Both modern consoles support remote play, a feature that lets you stream your game from your home setup.

If you’re looking to turn on the Xbox’s remote play feature, you need to access the Profile & System settings in the Xbox guide. From there, you need to navigate to the Devices & Connections menu and choose the Remote features option.

You’ll need to enable the remote features and put your console into sleep mode in order to pair your chosen remote play device. Remote play devices include smartphones, tablets and Windows computers.

According to recent reports, gamers who own a PlayStation 5 will need to follow similar steps to get remote play functioning on a mobile device. Within the PlayStation’s settings menu, navigate to the System tab and choose Remote Play. Toggle the Enable Remote Play option. From there, all of the necessary device pairing and gameplay setup will happen through the PS Remote Play app, which you can download on your handheld device.

Whether you own a PlayStation or an Xbox, you’ll want to ensure your console settings are tuned so it stays connected to the internet in rest mode. You’ll also need to enable the console to turn on via a network connection. These settings will allow you to start a remote play session anytime, even if you’ve already left your home.

If you’re using PlayStation’s remote play feature, you don’t have to fiddle around with gaming tablets or third-party handheld devices in order to find a comfortable way to play GTA 6. Sony’s PlayStation Portal is the perfect console accessory for natural gameplay, since it retains the DualShock controller design.

GTA 6 isn’t coming out on PC for a while still. That limits how many options you have when it comes to taking the game on the go with you. If (for whatever reason) you don’t have access to any remote play options, that leaves you with only the most inconvenient and unwieldy way to take the new crime simulator with you on the road.

You’ll have to lug around your PS5 or Xbox wherever you go to get in some GTA time – but hey, at least the gaming industry’s deteriorating respect for physical media means you won’t have to keep track of a disc.

Industry observers note that the PS5 Slim is probably the easiest current-gen console to carry with you, since the digital edition weighs less than 6 pounds. But you’re giving up the best possible performance available on the PS5 Pro.

Either way, you’ll be carrying around a large, expensive piece of hardware, so this option should only be considered if you really can’t get remote play functioning for whatever reason.

Industry observers note that microsoft’s video game ecosystem is huge, with Game Pass and streaming options available for PC players. But the Xbox brand isn’t offering gamers a cheat code to play GTA 6 on their beefy rigs (or any convenient handheld devices).

According to recent reports, GTA 6 is only available on Xbox consoles with Xbox Cloud Gaming at this time. The upside is that this option lets you play the boundary-pushing fresh game on the Xbox One, which is very close to being two console generations old.

At that point, you’re better off biting the bullet on a current-generation console and considering the available remote play options.

The company also uses license and supply arrangements with third parties to enter international markets like the UAE and Israel.

It has been revealed that in the 12 months ended Aug. 2, 2026, revenue reached nearly $11.1 billion, representing a growth rate of approximately 1.7%. Net income for this period was roughly $1.4 billion, resulting in a net margin of nearly 12.8%. The slower revenue growth suggests a period of normalization following years of rapid post-pandemic expansion.

Sources indicate that as of its February 2026 balance sheet, the debt-to-equity ratio was nearly 0.4x, showing the company uses relatively little debt compared to its equity. The current ratio was approximately 2.3x, suggesting a strong ability to cover short-term obligations. In the fiscal year ended Feb. 1, 2026, free cash flow reached close to $921.7 million.

It has been revealed that colgate-Palmolive faces significant exposure to international markets and fluctuations in foreign currency values. The firm deals with intense global competition from traditional rivals like Procter & Gamble (NYSE:PG) and newer private-label manufacturers. It also manages substantial legal uncertainty regarding ongoing talc-related litigation and operational risks from potential supply chain disruptions.

Lululemon Athletica manages heightened competition in the athletic apparel market, especially from imitation products. The organization is vulnerable to supply chain disruptions because its manufacturing and fabric sourcing are concentrated in the APAC region. Additionally, it faces reputational risks from pending securities class action lawsuits and sensitivity to changes in U.S. tariff policy.

Lululemon Athletica appears significantly cheaper than its peer, as it carries a lower Forward P/E and a lower P/S ratio, which measures sales over the past twelve months.

Valuation metrics include sourcing from Financial Modeling Prep (FMP) and may differ from other data providers.

I'd go with Colgate-Palmolive. It sells everyday products around the world and has raised its dividend for 63 straight years, a record built on things people buy in any economy. It holds the biggest share of the world's toothpaste market, and its Hill's pet food brand adds a second source of growth.

Last quarter, sales grew in nearly every region, emerging markets like India and Brazil led the way, and management raised its profit outlook. Costs are rising and U.S. shoppers are cautious, but those pressures are hitting the whole industry, and the rest of Colgate's business is still growing.

Industry observers note that to be fair to lululemon, it has a premium brand and $1.4 billion in cash. But sales are shrinking, with North American shoppers buying less at existing stores, and the company cut its full-year outlook in its latest report. What's more, a newly introduced CEO is still reshaping the leadership team. For investors who want to buy and hold into 2027 and beyond, Colgate offers steady growth and a dividend that gets bigger every year.

The Apple Watch was overdue for a chip upgrade, with Apple skipping any changes last year and not having any true performance upgrades since the S9.

I’m happy to report that the new S11 chip appears much faster and more capable than its predecessor, the S10.

Everyday tasks on Apple Watch Series 12 just feel fast. And Siri AI, a tentpole addition in watchOS 27, very much feels made for this latest hardware. Siri was sluggish on older hardware in my testing, but it performs much more like I’d hoped on Series 12.

Siri Recap ambiently takes notes on your conversations throughout your day and creates high-level Apple Intelligence–generated summaries that you can use later to jog your memory, so you can stay present in the moment.

Most of what Siri documents, I’ll never need to reference and it gets deleted automatically. But for those times I have trouble remembering a key piece of information, I’ve found Siri Recap a very convenient addition.

Apple Watch Series 12 offers largely the same battery life as Series 11, though it will last 25% longer for outdoor workouts.

Industry observers note that more battery is always nice, but I’m especially a fan of the faster charging available on Series 12. Here’s how it stacks up to Series 11:.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Just months after its release, Google is making its Spark agent free and officially renaming its capabilities “Tasks.” You can now toggle to it from the standard Gemini Chat setting.
  • According to recent reports, also: Ready for a Siri AI agent?
  • In a recent development, openAI offers its Dots agents as part of its $100 per month ChatGPT Pro tier, and Anthropic’s Claude Duet is available with paid plans, which start at $20 per month.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Just months after its release, Google is making its Spark agent free and officially renaming its capabilities “Tasks.” You can now toggle to it from the standard Gemini Chat setting. Reports show the rebrand started gradually in mid-October.

According to recent reports, also: Ready for a Siri AI agent? Apple under pressure to upgrade its assistant faster.

In a recent development, openAI offers its Dots agents as part of its $100 per month ChatGPT Pro tier, and Anthropic’s Claude Duet is available with paid plans, which start at $20 per month. That makes Tasks and Meta Muse — the latter was called the “worst AI agent for privacy” by ZDNET’s David Gewirtz — Big Tech’s most affordable personal agents on the market, though you’ll have to pay for more than five hours of access at a time.

Sources indicate that if Tasks sounds familiar, it should: The company already has a product called Google Tasks, which lets you turn emails into a checkable to-do list on the side of your inbox, among other places like Chat and Docs. This is the agentic version, obviously.

In a recent development, gewirtz, ZDNET’s AI tester-in-residence, wasn’t blown away by then-Spark when he tried it last month, but had reason to believe in its eventual improvement. It’s unclear whether Tasks is meaningfully different from Spark, aside from being out of beta.

Sources indicate that abilities aside, what sets Tasks apart here is cost. Dots and Duet haven’t exactly impressed thus far, so free alternatives don’t have a high bar to reach yet.

Also: I tested OpenAI Dot and Anthropic Duet for weeks.

During Gewirtz’s test, when the agent was part of his $20 per month Google AI Pro initiative, he used only 20% of the total five hours of usage on “four fairly substantial tests.” Without an AI plan, Gemini’s context window is 32k tokens.

Sources indicate that at launch in September, Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg noted Muse is “free to use for up to 100M tokens per week,” though Meta’s help center is not so explicit. As with most agentic products, more frequent users may want to buy more access, but more casual users now have two options to compare.

Sources indicate that AI companies are vying to hook customers with their various personal agents, and price and privacy are major factors to consider. Being free with limits, Muse and Tasks are perhaps geared toward a more apprehensive user who wants to try an agent, but isn’t giving it countless tasks to take on all day. Given Muse’s reputation, some may find Tasks a bit less aggressive or risky.

Also: Don’t use Muse? How Meta’s AI agent can still access your private messages.

As with other agents, Tasks, which runs on its newest Gemini 4 Hydrogen model, can handle a variety of jobs for you, from grocery shopping to booking appointments and analyzing your heating bill. Agents like these are designed for a chronically overwhelmed society trained by a reliance on tech to seek convenience and productivity in nearly every aspect of life.

The feature is free in the US, Canada, Korea, Japan, Australia, and India. US users can also start tasks by emailing or texting Gemini, and can have the agent call businesses for them (except in Indiana, Louisiana, Minnesota, Montana, and Nebraska).

Sources indicate that the change from Spark to Tasks comes just a day after Google retired Gems (which let you tailor Gemini to specific tasks), and converted existing Gems into Skills. The upcoming landing page for Tasks emphasizes personal finance and cost-cutting as a use case, positioning itself alongside personal finance features from Anthropic and OpenAI.

Recent findings suggest that “Put Gemini on the hunt for ways to save. Identify recurring expenses you no longer need, get alerts for your most-desired deals, and more,” the page reads.

AI agents remain a privacy and security risk, because of their ability to autonomously and proactively handle tasks like placing orders (which you can set spending caps for) and reviewing files.

Industry observers note that also: Want to try ChatGPT Wallet? Read OpenAI’s liability disclaimer.

Industry observers note that “You can adjust task settings, disconnect Google and third-party apps, or delete chat history anytime,’ Google’s blog on the release stated. Google’s new Memory summary feature for Gemini lets owners view and edit the personal info the chatbot has on them.

iOS 27.3 Could Bring the Redesigned Health App and a More Capable Siri AI to Your Device Soon

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1065 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cnet

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that apple debuted the second public beta of iOS 27.3 on Thursday, Nov.
  • Apple historically releases an iOS upgrade in December, so I expect iOS 27.3 to land on iPhones later this year.
  • Since this is a beta, I recommend downloading it on something other than your primary device.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that apple debuted the second public beta of iOS 27.3 on Thursday, Nov. 19, more than two months after the launch of the iPhone 18 Pro lineup and iOS 27. The headliner here is the return of the latest Health app: After briefly testing the redesigned Health app in an early iOS 27.2 beta, Apple has put the revamped app back in the recent beta cycle.

Apple historically releases an iOS upgrade in December, so I expect iOS 27.3 to land on iPhones later this year.

Since this is a beta, I recommend downloading it on something other than your primary device. This isn’t the final version of iOS 27.3, so the patch might be buggy and battery life may be short, so it’s best to keep those troubles on a secondary device.

Also, since this isn’t the final version, there could be more features to land on your iPhone when Apple releases 27.3.

Here are some features developers and beta testers can try now in the second iOS 27.3 beta.

Industry observers note that the redesigned Health app returns in the iOS 27.3 beta after Apple tested the feature in the iOS 27.2 beta process. Developers and beta testers can explore the refreshed app and see things like a fresh Longevity tab and your Health Age.

Apple wrote online that we can expect the redesigned Health app to land on devices later this year.

If developers and beta testers have an Apple Watch that is running the watchOS 27.3 beta as well as an iPhone running the iOS 27.3 beta, those folks can test out Apple’s Live Rewind and Siri Recap in Audio Intelligence.

Industry observers note that live Rewind allows you to pull up a text transcript of a conversation in the past 15 seconds on your Apple Watch, and Siri Recap can automatically give you a summary of meetings, conversations and other events. Live Rewind snippets are replaced by latest audio and then deleted, and Siri Recaps delete themselves after seven days if you don’t manually delete them sooner. However, you can also save both of these in the Siri app and export them to the Notes or Journal apps on your iPhone.

Sources indicate that while both Live Rewind and Siri Recap are automatically deleted over time, I’m uncomfortable with the ability to save snippets or recaps, which raises concerns about people recording my conversations without my knowledge. Even if Audio Intelligence just summarizes what I remarked, I still find both features creepy.

And while I recognize the utility for certain groups of people, I also think it’s better to just, y’know… talk to someone instead of asking your watch what they just said.

Siri AI gets a huge update in the iOS 27.3 beta. The feature can now do more actions in supported apps, like Apple Music and Messages. For example, if you go into Apple Music, you can ask Siri to create a playlist for you, and in Messages, you can ask Siri to schedule, edit or unsend messages. If you open an app and ask Siri what it can do, the digital assistant should give you some examples of its capabilities.

Industry observers note that you can also use Siri in Safari to scan an entire webpage — even parts of the page that aren’t in your direct view — to give you helpful information. So if you are looking at a menu online, you can ask Siri to find the gluten-free or vegetarian options.

The beta also brings Siri AI to traditional Chinese, Vietnamese, Turkish and Norwegian.

Sources indicate that in the latest iOS 27.3 beta, developers and beta testers can find video podcasts in the Apple TV app, as well as in the Podcasts app. You can find video podcasts by going into the app, tapping Home across the bottom of your screen and scrolling down to the Video Podcasts section.

This means you can watch a video podcast in the Apple TV app on your iPhone while commuting, and then you can finish that video later on an Apple TV 4K or another device with access to Apple TV.

It has been revealed that each workout recommends exercises, reps, sets and weights in order to help you meet your goals. And if you’re unfamiliar with an exercise, you can also watch video tutorials to see how to perform that exercise.

It has been revealed that standBy mode also gets an upgrade in the iOS 27.3 beta. In the beta, you can add full weather and calendar slides to the mode and choose from more colors.

Apple introduced StandBy mode alongside iOS 17, and it was one of my favorite iPhone features. I’m happy Apple is finally showing it some love and adding more features and capabilities so it feels more like a home or desk hub.

If you’re a fan of dark mode, the iOS 27.3 beta has a treat for you. The beta gives you a new setting in Safari called Adaptive Dark Mode. When enabled, it forces dark mode onto webpages in Safari that may not have a dark mode option otherwise.

Here’s where to find the option.

1. Tap Settings.2. Tap Apps.3. Tap Safari.4. Tap Adaptive Dark Mode.5. Tap On.

In a recent development, if you have an iPhone Duo and are running the iOS 27.3 beta, you have new options to lock and unlock your device. In the beta, you can enable your device to lock simply by closing the Duo. You can find this option in Settings and within the Display & Brightness menu.

According to recent reports, next, people with the Duo can unlock the device using that phone’s front camera and without opening the foldable. You will have had to recently unlocked your device with Touch ID or your passcode. You can find this option in Settings and in the Touch ID & Passcode menu.

Sources indicate that those are a few of the fresh features developers can try now with the second beta of iOS 27.3. Apple has not said when exactly it will release iOS 27.3 to the general public, but we expect it to land on devices before the end of the year.

Nvidia Stock Plunge Wipes Out Nearly $500 Billion in One Day as SEC Reportedly Probes Its Accounting

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (709 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fool

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Shares of Nvidia (NVDA -14.01%) fell 14% on Friday afternoon, to less than $126, after Reuters reported that the Securities and Exchange Commission is investigating the chipmaker's accounting.
  • Sources indicate that zoom out and the damage is even bigger.
  • Here's what we know, and what investors should make of it.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Jonathan Ponciano – Nov 20, 2026 at 4:07PM EST.

Nvidia's terrible month just got worse.

Shares of Nvidia (NVDA -14.01%) fell 14% on Friday afternoon, to less than $126, after Reuters reported that the Securities and Exchange Commission is investigating the chipmaker's accounting. The drop erased roughly $491 billion in market value in a single session, taking Nvidia from about $3.52 trillion to about $3.03 trillion.

Sources indicate that zoom out and the damage is even bigger. Nvidia closed at a record $239.24 on Oct. 6. At Friday's price, the stock is down about 48% from that high, and the company has lost about $2.7 trillion in value in just six weeks.

Here's what we know, and what investors should make of it.

The Wall Street Journal first reported on Tuesday that the SEC was investigating Nvidia but couldn't say what the probe was about. On Friday, Reuters, citing two people briefed on the matter, reported that the agency's enforcement staff are examining potential accounting challenges at the manufacturer.

Recent findings suggest that many questions remain unanswered. Reuters couldn't determine when the inquiry began or which accounting practices are under review. The SEC declined to comment, and Nvidia didn't immediately respond. Keep in mind that the SEC investigates plenty of companies that are never charged with anything.

The stock was already having a bad day before the report: shares were down more than 6% earlier in the session amid a broad sell-off in AI stocks.

The probe adds to a pile of problems. Nvidia co-founder Jensen Huang resigned as CEO on Nov. 11 following revelations about his personal relationships, including with a woman U.S. authorities suspect of spying for China, which China denies. The Justice Department is also reviewing Nvidia's planned $12.9 billion purchase of Hugging Face, according to Reuters.

Sources indicate that two areas could draw scrutiny. The first is how Nvidia reports where its sales come from. The organization breaks out revenue by where customers are headquartered, rather than where they're billed. On that basis, about 63% of last quarter's revenue came from U.S.-based customers. The Financial Times has reported that Nvidia made the switch as sales billed to Singapore approached half of its total, a bad look with Southeast Asia having become a hub for chips smuggled into China.

The second is how Nvidia helps its customers pay for its chips. On Tuesday's earnings call, interim CEO Colette Kress said Nvidia's guarantees totaled $118 billion at the end of the quarter, including $105 billion of credit support tied to a single data center campus. These guarantees are the kind of disclosure the SEC is watching closely at AI companies. When a chipmaker helps fund the projects that buy its chips, it's harder to tell how much demand would exist on its own.

None of this has shown up in the numbers yet. Nvidia's revenue jumped 103% to $115.8 billion last quarter, and the company expects about $130 billion this quarter. Management even raised its growth forecast for next fiscal year to about 75%. At about $126, the stock trades at roughly 12 times last quarter's adjusted earnings of $2.68 per share on an annualized basis, cheap for a company growing this fast.

But cheap can get cheaper. Accounting questions hit at the heart of what investors pay for: trust in the numbers. Until Nvidia names a permanent CEO and the SEC's focus becomes clearer, the stock could stay volatile, even after a 48% drop.

Industry observers note that for long-term investors who already own Nvidia, there's no need to panic-sell on a report about an investigation. For anyone thinking of buying, it's smarter to wait for more clarity, or to build a position slowly, than to bet that the worst is over. There are plenty of other semiconductor stocks without a cloud of investigations hanging over them.
