💡 Key Takeaways
  • Hilton is making a major play in South Florida with its Signia by Hilton Diplomat Beach Resort.
  • Industry observers note that the resort caters primarily to business and group travelers (it’s attached to a massive events space), but it’s also a strong option for vacationers looking for some R&R.
  • Room rates typically run $300 to $600 a night, depending on the season, but you can also use Hilton Honors benefits to make your stay more affordable.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Hilton is making a major play in South Florida with its Signia by Hilton Diplomat Beach Resort. The massive 1,000-room property — which underwent an $80 million renovation before opening under the Signia Hilton brand in May 2026 — sits on the beach in Hollywood, Florida, just outside of Fort Lauderdale.

Industry observers note that the resort caters primarily to business and group travelers (it’s attached to a massive events space), but it’s also a strong option for vacationers looking for some R&R. The main downside: The location isn’t great if your trip primarily revolves around off-property excursions, dining and nightlife.

Room rates typically run $300 to $600 a night, depending on the season, but you can also use Hilton Honors benefits to make your stay more affordable. There’s also a resort fee of $59 per night — but Hilton waives that when you book using Hilton points.

According to recent reports, hilton covered the cost of my stay for two nights, but the opinions in this review are my own. Here’s what guests can expect at this oceanfront resort.

Since the Signia by Hilton Diplomat Beach Resort is part of Hilton Honors, there are several ways to book a stay there.

If you’re using Hilton points, expect to pay 70,000 to 80,000 points a night when standard rooms are available. Hilton elite status — a benefit you can earn by holding any Hilton Honors credit card — gets you the fifth-night-free perk, where you stay for at least five nights but pay for four when booking with points.

For example, if you were to stay five nights at 80,000 points a night, you’d pay 320,000 points total, bringing down your average nightly rate to 64,000 points.

You can also book using Hilton’s generous free night certificates, which can be used at almost any property in the portfolio. If you hold the Hilton Honors American Express Aspire Card, you automatically get a certificate each year. It’s also possible to earn certificates through reaching spending thresholds on the card and on the Hilton Honors American Express Surpass® Card. Terms apply.

Industry observers note that make sure to check the cash rate against the points rate to make sure you’re getting good value from your redemption. NerdWallet values Hilton points at 0.4 cent apiece.

Recent findings suggest that for cash bookings of two nights or more, you might consider using The Hotel Collection via American Express’ travel portal for eligible cardholders. Eligible bookings come with benefits like a $100 property credit and other amenities subject to availability, including a room upgrade, early check-in and late checkout.

Keep in mind that third-party bookings typically don’t earn Hilton points or count toward elite status qualification.

It’s hard to miss the Signia by Hilton Diplomat Beach Resort, with its signature H-shaped facade and sleek white-and-glass exterior.

According to recent reports, stepping into the hotel, I was immediately struck by the lush greenery filling the entrance and indoor courtyard. The grand lobby has soaring glass ceilings, giving the space a greenhouse feel, although the strong air conditioning keeps you cool.

In a recent development, despite its massive size, it doesn’t have a sprawling layout, which I appreciated. Everything is close together, and you can walk from the check-in counter to any of the indoor restaurants in under a minute.

It has been revealed that I stayed in an oceanfront suite with a balcony, which was spacious and had a fun beachy vibe. To get to the rooms, you’ll need to use either the north or south tower elevator banks.

In the living room, there was a large sitting area featuring a TV, a couch, an accent chair and a four-person high-top table.

Although I didn’t spend too much time on the balcony — the October balminess was a bit too much for me — I enjoyed stepping out each morning to admire the view.

The bedroom had a king bed with extremely comfortable bedding and an oversized chair that was a great spot to relax and read a book by the window.

The bathroom was spacious, featuring a shower and a separate tub (something every room has).

Even the standard room I toured felt roomy. I liked that it shared similar elements with the suite, including the oversized lounge chair.

This is what you’d normally get when booking a room at the cheapest points price.

Sources indicate that there are several dining venues on the property, ranging from a grab-and-go cafe to a high-end steakhouse. It is a luxury resort, so expect the prices to reflect that.

For breakfast, you can head to Palmea Kitchen, which is also open for lunch. I had the breakfast buffet, which offered a nice spread of classics, from hot food items and pastries to cold cuts and smoked salmon.

If you don’t have time for a sit-down breakfast, you can head next door to The Press, which offers made-to-order and grab-and-go food options throughout the day. You can also get smoothies, juices, snacks, pastries and other sweet treats.

The Canteen is another grab-and-go option that also sells snacks, drinks, souvenirs and sundries, similar to a convenience store.

According to recent reports, for lunch and dinner, try Solara. It doesn’t have a traditional restaurant feel, as it’s mostly an indoor-outdoor bar space. One side connects to the lobby, while the other side faces the Solara adults-only pool.

It serves a lunch menu, as well as a substantial bar food menu that’s available late into the night.

It has been revealed that you can also eat at Playa Beach Bar & Grill, a beachside restaurant serving Latin-inspired cuisine. I enjoyed spending a lazy lunch there and watching the waves crash onto the shore.

For a fancy sit-down dinner, go to Diplomat Prime, the property’s steakhouse. We had a group dinner at the restaurant, and the meats were, of course, the highlight. But don’t sleep on the seafood, which was also delicious.

One of the best parts of the Dip, as it’s affectionately known, is its location right on the beach. Guests can access the stretch of beach directly adjacent to the property. But it’s not a private beach, so you might encounter crowds.

I didn’t spend any time on the beach itself — it was extremely windy while I was there — but the hotel’s resort fee includes amenities like a beach lounge (umbrella not included), a daily one-hour kayak or paddleboard rental, and beachfront yoga classes.

If you don’t want to get sand everywhere, you can head to one of the three pool options: the adults-only Solara pool, the family-friendly lagoon pool and the Verandah Social Club for those 21 and older (requires paid access).

Sources indicate that the family-friendly lagoon spans the length of the property and runs beneath the Solara pool. It also has its own hot tub.

I spent an afternoon in a cabana at the Verandah Social Club, which has some smaller plunge pools and a hot tub.

I appreciated the attentive service from the staff there, who constantly checked on whether guests needed anything.

If you’re looking for other ways to stay active, head to the two-story fitness center, featuring a variety of equipment like free weights, exercise bikes, a rowing machine and treadmills.

Industry observers note that next door, you’ll find the spa and wellness center. I had a relaxing massage that incorporated hot stones and aromatherapy.

The locker rooms come with a sauna and steam room, although I wished there were more amenities like a hot tub and cold plunge.

It has been revealed that one of the resort fee inclusions is complimentary high-intensity interval training workout classes at the gym across the street. I signed up for an early morning class. The instructor was friendly, and it was a great way to start my day.

Other amenities include a complimentary one-hour e-bike rental each day, as well as a kids’ club with various activities (but drop-off fees apply).

I had a fantastic stay at this resort, but I’d recommend it for a specific traveler.

In a recent development, if you’re planning to stay on-property your entire trip, it’s a great option. That’s probably why it’s such a popular convention hotel, since everything you need is easily accessible.

I loved the hotel’s design, including the jungle-like atmosphere in the lobby, and I found the dining options to be tasty, albeit pricey.

But if your trip revolves around visiting Miami attractions, you’ll likely want to stay closer to the action.

Latest Update: Trust Is The Upcoming Battleground For Customer Engagement

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (942 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Forbes

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • James Garvert is the EVP of Fraud & Communications Solutions for TransUnion.
  • Industry observers note that ​Engaging with consumers has never been more essential, or more difficult.
  • It has been revealed that every interaction depends on trust, yet consumers are more hesitant than ever to engage.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

James Garvert is the EVP of Fraud & Communications Solutions for TransUnion.

Industry observers note that ​Engaging with consumers has never been more essential, or more difficult. Amid the meteoric rise of AI-enabled scams, call spoofing and social engineering attacks, the challenges organizations face when trying to reach consumers seem insurmountable.

It has been revealed that every interaction depends on trust, yet consumers are more hesitant than ever to engage. Many of the traditional warning signs consumers were trained to recognize have disappeared—consumers are on edge.

And with good reason: It’s a jungle out there.

It has been revealed that in our recent global study, “61% of business leaders ranked fraud among the risks with the greatest potential business impact, ahead of cybersecurity breaches, compliance, customer churn, operational cost and reputational risk. More concerning, 58% said they’re very or extremely concerned fraud is evolving faster than their organizations’ abilities to detect and prevent it.”.

Historically, organizations have viewed fraud and engaging with customers as separate disciplines. But today’s threat environment makes it clear they’re deeply interconnected. In many cases, the communication channel itself—whether a phone call, text message, email or mobile app interaction—provides the first indication that fraud may be occurring.

Recent findings suggest that consumers don’t experience fraud, identity and communication challenges as separate issues. To them, it’s one experience, one problem. It’s a trust problem that’s reshaping the customer journey. In fact, 69% of consumers say they would switch vendors for stronger security.

Trust has become the foundation for both customer engagement and fraud prevention.

Sources indicate that at our recent Fraud & Communications Summit in Chicago, keynote speaker Matt O’Neill, a former U.S. Secret Service Special Agent and recipient of Gold and Silver Awards for distinguished service, shared insights from years spent working undercover as a banker, broker, money launderer and other personas. In these roles, he led multinational investigations into crypto-laundering networks and dark web marketplaces.

According to O’Neill, fraudsters are winning because fraud has evolved into a highly organized industry. He explained that scam operations now function much like large multinational corporations. Scam compounds are similar to call centers, complete with organizational structures, performance quotas, shift schedules and human resources departments. Unfortunately, many of these compounds operate under sophisticated criminal networks and employ workers who have been trafficked.

According to recent reports, at the same time, the barrier to entry into the fraud world has never been lower. AI enables fraudsters to create convincing scams at scale in virtually any language, including cloned voices, deepfake videos and personalized social engineering campaigns. And it’s cheap.​.

Sources indicate that the consequences of eroding trust extend well beyond fraud losses. Organizations often experience:.

• Reduced marketing effectiveness.

Ironically, the industries and brands most trusted by consumers are frequently among the most targeted by fraudsters, with the highest fraud instances related to auto lending, bank-issued and retail credit cards and unsecured personal lending.

According to Edelman, trust now rivals price and quality as a primary factor influencing consumer decision-making. Research reveals that “77% of consumers cited confidence their personal data is secure as the most key feature when choosing whom to transact with online.”.

Organizations can strengthen trust by approaching fraud prevention and customer communications as a unified strategy.

In a recent development, traditional fraud controls were designed for predictable attacks. Today’s fraudsters adapt swiftly, vary their tactics and coordinate attacks across multiple channels and sessions. Identity verification remains important, but it only confirms who someone claims to be. It doesn’t determine whether the current interaction should be trusted.

Here’s where identity verification falls short:.

• KYC (Know Your Customer) controls are often strongest at onboarding, not throughout the customer lifecycle.

• Devices, behaviors and risk profiles change over time.

• Credentials can be compromised after verification.

• Synthetic identities can appear legitimate on paper.

The most vital fraud signal is often not a single event. Any single signal can be manipulated or generate false positives. It’s the story that unfolds throughout an interaction. It emerges through relationships among people, devices, accounts, entities and sessions.

As if it wasn’t hard enough, AI has turbocharged fraud. In addition, labeling identified threats as AI-driven remains a challenge. That’s because it’s difficult to build comprehensive strategies with upcoming AI fraud models evolving so rapidly.

Sources indicate that while fraud practitioners know when an account was taken over, there’s presently no label for how it was taken over and whether AI drove the attack. As a result, the AI-attributed training set doesn’t exist yet for tracking that fraud, and detection stays anchored to heuristics and analyst judgment.

To be able to engage effectively with consumers and prevent fraud, organizations must adopt continuous authentication and layered risk strategies.

• Develop a comprehensive strategy—don’t address fraud in silos across your organization.

• Form strategic partnerships with your cyber teams.

• Correlate identity, device, behavioral and contextual signals in real time.

Recent findings suggest that the process is straightforward: Collect. Correlate. Score. Decide.

It has been revealed that every phone call, text message, email and digital transaction represents a trust moment. Customers want confidence the organization contacting them is legitimate and their information and transactions are protected. Simply asking consumers to “trust us” is no longer enough.

Verified identity, authenticated communications and real-time risk intelligence are becoming the foundation of trust in a digital-first world.

According to recent reports, the future isn’t reactive fraud mitigation. It’s proactive trust at the point of interaction, by orchestrating identity, risk and communications intelligence across every customer interaction.

There are six communities, including two reserved for Alaska and Hawaii residents. The other four are open to members regardless of where they live. But don’t get caught up in the community names. The best choice for you may depend more on your travel plans than the groupings suggest.

Here’s how to decide which Atmos Community best fits your travel patterns.

» Learn more: The guide to Atmos Rewards.

Atmos Communities are like groups within the Atmos Rewards program that offer additional benefits based on different travel interests.

In a recent development, they’re free to join for Atmos Rewards members. Four communities are available to all members, while community Club 49 is reserved for Alaska residents and community Huaka’i by Hawaiian is reserved for Hawaii residents.

It has been revealed that you can belong to only one community at a time and switch communities once per calendar year. Consider your upcoming travel plans before choosing.

Industry observers note that each Atmos Community has a list of 10 destinations where members can earn bonus points and status points. Although the destinations differ by community, the rewards structure is the same.

Sources indicate that through Dec. 31, 2027, members can earn up to 10,000 bonus points and 10,000 status points by visiting qualifying destinations.

Here’s how many points you’ll earn as you reach each milestone:.

Visit one destination, earn 100 status and bonus points.

Visit two destinations, earn 200 status and bonus points.

Visit three destinations, earn 300 status and bonus points.

Visit four destinations, earn 400 status and bonus points.

Visit five destinations, earn 500 status and bonus points.

Visit six destinations, earn 750 status and bonus points.

Visit seven destinations, earn 1,000 status and bonus points.

Visit eight destinations, earn 1,250 status and bonus points.

Visit nine destinations, earn 2,500 status and bonus points.

Visit 10 destinations, earn 3,000 status and bonus points.

The first member of each community to visit all 10 qualifying destinations during the challenge period will also earn 100,000 bonus points.

Recent findings suggest that new lists of qualifying destinations for each community take effect on Jan. 1, 2028.

Here’s a closer look at the six communities, their benefits and the destinations eligible for bonus points.

Global Locals is geared toward frequent international travelers. Benefits include:.

Earn 10% more status points toward Atmos elite status on flights that begin and/or end outside the U.S., including award flights.

Bitcoin broke below the psychologically important $60,000 level, while Ethereum and Solana experienced even steeper declines as investors continued to retreat from riskier assets.

It has been revealed that as of early evening, Bitcoin (BTC -8.48%) had plunged 6.01% to $58,186.39, while Ethereum (ETH -9.38%) tumbled 9.03% to $1,596.72 and Solana (SOL -8.28%) declined 8.02% to $67.21. Deteriorating investor risk appetite continued to weigh on cryptocurrencies Friday as concerns over interest rates, elevated valuations, and tighter financial conditions fueled a broad sell-off across global markets. With the Nasdaq plunging more than 5%, investors appeared increasingly focused on raising cash and reducing exposure to riskier assets.

Recent findings suggest that the simultaneous decline in stocks, gold, and cryptocurrencies suggests selling pressure is extending beyond individual markets. Rather than simply rotating capital between asset classes, investors appear to be reducing their overall risk exposure, leaving cryptocurrencies particularly vulnerable as liquidity conditions continue to deteriorate.

Spot cryptocurrency ETFs suffered steep losses on Friday, mirroring the broader sell-off in digital assets. The iShares Bitcoin Trust ETF (IBIT -5.87%) fell 5.87%, while the Fidelity Wise Origin Bitcoin Fund (FBTC -6.16%) declined 5.97%. Meanwhile, the iShares Ethereum Trust ETF (ETHA -9.16%) plunged 9.16%, reflecting Ethereum's particularly sharp decline.

Bitcoin's break below $60,000 marks another significant deterioration in the cryptocurrency market's technical outlook. With Ethereum approaching $1,500 and Solana falling below $70, several major cryptocurrencies are now trading near levels that could determine whether the current bear market extends into 2027. If selling pressure persists, investors could see another round of latest lows before a sustainable recovery takes shape.

Beyond price action, the broader withdrawal of capital from digital assets presents a more fundamental challenge. Bitcoin ETF outflows have reportedly exceeded $2.5 billion in 2026, while the simultaneous sell-off across stocks, gold, and cryptocurrencies suggests investors are prioritizing liquidity over risk-taking. Without renewed capital inflows, even sharp relief rallies may struggle to develop into sustained recoveries.

Looking ahead, investors should watch whether Bitcoin can reclaim $60,000, Ethereum can recover above $1,800, and Solana can establish support above $70. Improving ETF flows, stabilizing prices, and a recovery in broader financial markets would provide more convincing evidence that conditions are improving. Until then, the combination of weakening demand and unfavorable macroeconomic conditions leaves cryptocurrencies vulnerable to further declines heading into year-end.

#39419. SpaceX Aims to Spend $2.8 Billion on Gas Turbines. Here’s What That Much Natural Gas Demand Means for Pipeline Investors.

📅 20 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (764 w)
📖 Baca
Business & Policy ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Fool ↗ Open Full Page

SpaceX Aims to Spend $2.8 Billion on Gas Turbines. Here’s What That Much Natural Gas Demand Means for Pipeline Investors.

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (764 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fool

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that when SpaceX (SPCX -7.69%) went public in June, it disclosed $2.8 billion in purchase commitments for gas turbines and related equipment in its IPO prospectus.
  • Industry observers note that that massive investment in behind-the-meter (BTM) natural gas connections, which generate electricity on the customer's side of the electric meter rather than going through an energy provider, is a bright green flag for the natural gas market.
  • Industry observers note that an easy way to profit from that secular trend is through midstream pipeline companies, which deliver the natural gas to those data centers.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Leo Sun – Nov 20, 2026 at 4:55PM EST.

Industry observers note that when SpaceX (SPCX -7.69%) went public in June, it disclosed $2.8 billion in purchase commitments for gas turbines and related equipment in its IPO prospectus. SpaceX is purchasing those turbines to power its own data centers and factories.

Industry observers note that that massive investment in behind-the-meter (BTM) natural gas connections, which generate electricity on the customer's side of the electric meter rather than going through an energy provider, is a bright green flag for the natural gas market. U.S. data centers already generate over 40% of their electricity from natural gas, according to the International Energy Agency (IEA). That percentage could continue to rise as the cloud and AI markets expand.

Industry observers note that an easy way to profit from that secular trend is through midstream pipeline companies, which deliver the natural gas to those data centers. Pipeline operators charge companies "tolls" to use their infrastructure, so they're well-insulated from volatile commodity prices. Instead, they simply need the resources to keep flowing through their pipes to generate stable profits. Most pipeline companies also return lots of cash to their investors through high dividends and distributions.

As demand for natural gas rises, pipeline companies will need to expand their infrastructure to handle the increased volumes. Those investments could compress their near-term margins, but they'll support their long-term growth. Let's see which of these pipeline operators will benefit the most from the rapid growth of the cloud infrastructure and AI data center markets.

According to recent reports, the Williams Companies (WMB -2.75%) operates more than 32,000 miles of pipeline across 24 states. It owns Transco, the largest natural gas pipeline in the U.S., which connects the Gulf Coast to the Atlantic seaboard. Its pipelines handle roughly a third of all natural gas produced in the United States.

NYSE · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

Sources indicate that unlike more diversified pipeline companies, Williams generates most of its revenue by gathering, processing, storing, and transporting natural gas. A smaller percentage of revenue comes from natural gas liquids (NGLs), crude oil handling services, and electricity generation.

Recent findings suggest that from 2025 to 2028, analysts expect Williams' EPS to grow at a 12% CAGR. It still looks reasonably valued at 26 times next year's earnings, and it could command an even higher valuation if the data center market heats up again.

Williams has raised its dividend annually over the past nine years, and it's paid continuous dividends for the past 52 years. It at the moment pays a forward yield of 3.2%, and its low payout ratio of 82% gives it ample room for future dividend hikes.

Energy Transfer (ET -2.62%) operates more than 140,000 miles of pipeline across 44 states. It transports crude oil, natural gas, natural gas liquids (NGLs), and other refined products through its pipelines. It also exports NGLs through its marine export terminals.

TXSE · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

Energy Transfer's pipelines transport about 30% of the natural gas produced in the United States. It generates only approximately 40% of its adjusted earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortization (EBITDA) from natural gas, which makes it less of a direct play on natural gas than Williams. Still, Energy Transfer is more exposed to that market than many of its peers.

It has been revealed that unlike Williams, which operates as a traditional corporation, Energy Transfer is a master limited partnership (MLP) that treats its investors as partners rather than shareholders. MLPs pay distributions -- much of which are classified as a "return of capital" for more tax-efficient returns -- rather than traditional dividends. That strategy enables it to pay a high forward yield of 7.2%, but its investors must file an additional K-1 form (for MLPs) with their taxes each year.

Sources indicate that from 2025 to 2028, analysts expect Energy Transfer's earnings per unit (EPU) to grow at a 13% CAGR. It trades at just 12 times next's year's EPU, and that low valuation should limit its downside even if the cloud and AI markets cool off over the next few years.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • The average interest rate on a 30-year, fixed-rate mortgage dropped to 7.24% APR, according to rates provided to NerdWallet by Zillow.
  • In a recent development, A significant drop is eye-catching, but you should consider mortgage interest rates' overall direction, not just what's going on today.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Mortgage rates dropped today, but anything above 7% still puts pressure on home buyers’ budgets.

The average interest rate on a 30-year, fixed-rate mortgage dropped to 7.24% APR, according to rates provided to NerdWallet by Zillow. This is 14 basis points lower than yesterday and three basis points lower than a week ago. (A basis point is one one-hundredth of a percentage point.).

In a recent development, A significant drop is eye-catching, but you should consider mortgage interest rates' overall direction, not just what's going on today. While the economy never sleeps, markets are closed on the weekends. The rates you see Friday are unlikely to change much (if at all) until Monday.

Here are the average APRs we're seeing today, as well as movement over the past month for context:.

» Take the next step: Compare mortgage rates from NerdWallet’s top lenders.

According to recent reports, mortgage rates are constantly changing, since a major part of how rates are set depends on reactions to new inflation reports, job numbers, Fed meetings, global news ... you name it. For example, even tiny changes in the bond market can shift mortgage pricing.

Industry observers note that next week, the Nerds are waiting for the Personal Consumption Expenditures (PCE) price index, due out Wednesday. It's the Federal Reserve's preferred measure of inflation, so investors will be watching closely. The Fed doesn't set mortgage rates, but lenders anticipate its decisions, so mortgage rates often move before the Fed acts. Stubbornly high inflation is a substantial reason why we’re seeing upward pressure on mortgage rates right now.

Industry observers note that if PCE highlights inflation comes in hotter than expected, mortgage rates could climb as markets anticipate further Fed rate hikes. (An increase to the federal funds rate is already widely expected at the Fed’s Dec. 8-9 meeting.) A cooler reading could ease some pressure on mortgage rates for now.

I’m not getting my hopes up too high for meaningfully lower inflation, though. Last week's Producer Price Index highlighted wholesale inflation climbed 6.5% over the past year — its fastest pace in four years. Wholesale inflation measures the price businesses pay for things. When businesses’ costs go up, they could pass those along to consumers in the form of higher prices — keeping the flames of inflation alive.

Whether Wednesday's PCE brings relief or another helping of bad inflation news, we'll know before the turkey hits the table on Thursday.

Refinancing might make sense if today’s rates are at least 0.5 to 0.75 of a percentage point lower than your current rate (and if you plan to stay in your home long enough to break even on closing costs).

With rates where they are right now, you may want to start considering a refi if your current rate is around 7.74% or higher.

Recent findings suggest that also consider your goals: Are you trying to lower your monthly payment, shorten your loan term or turn home equity into cash? For example, you might be more comfortable with paying a higher rate for a cash-out refinance than you would for a rate-and-term refinance, so long as the overall costs are lower than if you kept your original mortgage and added a HELOC or home equity loan.

If you're looking for a lower rate, use NerdWallet's refinance calculator to estimate savings and understand how long it would take to break even on the costs of refinancing.

Sources indicate that » Time to refi? Compare refinance rates from NerdWallet’s top lenders.

There is no universal “right” time to start shopping — what matters is whether you can comfortably afford a mortgage now at today’s rates.

It has been revealed that if the answer is yes, don’t get too hung up on whether you could be missing out on lower rates later; you can refinance down the road. Focus on getting preapproved, comparing lender offers, and understanding what monthly payment works for your budget.

NerdWallet’s affordability calculator can help you estimate your potential monthly payment. If a fresh home isn’t in the cards right now, there are still things you can do to strengthen your buyer profile. Take this time to pay down existing debts and build your down payment savings. Not only will this free up more cash flow for a future mortgage payment, it can also get you a better interest rate when you’re ready to buy.

» Is now a good time to buy? See NerdWallet’s analysis.

If you already have a quote you’re happy with, you should consider locking your mortgage rate, especially if your lender offers a float-down option. A float-down lets you take advantage of a better rate if the market drops during your lock period.

Rate locks protect you from increases while your loan is processed, and with the market forever bouncing around, that peace of mind can be worth it.

🤓 Nerdy Reminder: Rates can change daily, and even hourly. If you’re happy with the deal you have, it’s okay to commit.

#39417. When To End A Technology Pilot: 19 Warning Signs

📅 20 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 7m • 📚 Deep Dive (1325 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚠️ Warning 🌐 Forbes ↗ Open Full Page

When To End A Technology Pilot: 19 Warning Signs

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1325 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Forbes

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that technology pilots give organizations an opportunity to test latest solutions on a limited scale, evaluate their potential and identify challenges before committing to a broader rollout.
  • In a recent development, for tech leaders, the challenge is distinguishing between setbacks that can be addressed by adjusting a pilot’s scope or timeline and more fundamental problems that call its viability into question.
  • A pilot without success criteria is not a pilot.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that technology pilots give organizations an opportunity to test latest solutions on a limited scale, evaluate their potential and identify challenges before committing to a broader rollout. But not every pilot warrants further investment, and knowing when to end one can be just as key as knowing when to expand it.

In a recent development, for tech leaders, the challenge is distinguishing between setbacks that can be addressed by adjusting a pilot’s scope or timeline and more fundamental problems that call its viability into question. Below, members of Forbes Technology Council share warning signs that indicate it’s time to end a technology pilot rather than extend it, redesign it or move it into production.

A pilot without success criteria is not a pilot. Defining boundaries and expectations, and, importantly, being transparent, are critical to a pilot’s success. Owners should also share any uncertainty during the pilot instead of waiting for it to pivot or improve. - Arunava Sen, Tata Communications America Inc.

A clear sign is when the pilot team cannot tell you what the technology accessed, what decisions it made, or what data it touched. If you cannot answer those questions in a controlled environment (test group), you will not answer them in production. - Michael Nicosia, Salt Security.

According to recent reports, forbes Technology Council is an invitation-only community for world-class CIOs, CTOs and technology executives. Do I qualify?

One sign a technology pilot shouldn’t progress doesn’t involve the fresh tech itself but the tools teams already work with. If teams are working in siloed workflows with tools that don’t collaborate with one another, introducing new technology can drive up costs, increase complexity and hurt productivity. Connected tools and workflows are integral to the success of any new tech deployment. - Usman Shuja, Bluebeam.

It has been revealed that end a pilot when its success depends on hand-curated data that won’t exist in production. If someone cleaned the dataset, resolved definitions and fixed edge cases for the pilot, and no one owns doing that at scale in production, extending or redesigning the product in production won’t help. In many cases, technology isn’t the problem; the foundation is. Ask not whether the pilot worked, but what it worked on. - Prakash Reddy, Okta.

If the pilot only works while its champion is in the room or while the vendor quietly does manual work behind the scenes, you’ve tested enthusiasm, not technology. Hand it to a team that didn’t build it for 30 days. If results collapse, you’d be pushing a dependency into production, not a tool. End it and keep the learnings. - Damian Wasserman, BEON.tech.

When the team stops asking what we learned and starts asking when we get to stop, that’s the sign. A pilot without defined success criteria is avoidance. If you can’t name the specific business result it was supposed to prove or disprove, extending it won’t help. End it, define the outcome you actually need, and redesign around that from the start. - Ali Alkhafaji, APPLY.

Industry observers note that organizations should end a technology pilot when they have full visibility of the tool’s usage and cost metrics but still cannot connect either to a meaningful business outcome. Adoption alone is not enough without a clear path to measurable value, and extending the pilot risks turning experimentation into ongoing spend without a business case. - Conal Gallagher, Flexera.

In a recent development, A clear sign is when the people who were supposed to benefit stop asking about it. Pilots drag on because the sponsors like the idea, not because users need it. If the pilot group has quietly gone back to their old way of working and nobody complains when the tool goes down, there’s nothing to extend. Name the lesson, thank the team and end it. - Hastimal Jangid, Coozmoo Digital Solutions, Inc.

According to recent reports, A pilot should be reconsidered when it performs well in a demo but can’t prove that it solves a real business problem. AI makes it easy to add capabilities, but more features don’t always mean more value. Teams need clear measures of success and feedback loops to understand what’s working and what’s not before investing further. - Tony Grout, M-Files.

A clear sign to end a technology pilot is when it repeatedly fails to demonstrate measurable business value despite validated assumptions and reasonable adjustments. If the solution cannot deliver meaningful ROI, operational efficiency or strategic impact, extending it only increases sunk costs. Strong leadership means knowing when to stop, not just when to scale. - Kameshwar Singh, Cohesity.

End a pilot if no effort was spent defining the vision and how value will be realized at scale. That’s like building a bridge from both ends without deciding where it should meet. - Venky Ramesh, LatentView Analytics.

Sources indicate that A pilot should end when success depends on conditions that production will never have: handpicked data, expert customers, manual fixes, privileged integrations or constant vendor support. If removing that scaffolding collapses the value case, extending the pilot only perfects the illusion. The real test is not, “Does it work?” but, “Does it still create measurable value when exposed to ordinary users, messy data, real constraints and an ordinary day?” - Nicola Sfondrini, PWC.

Sources indicate that end a pilot when making the technology operable, reliable and governable outweighs its business value. If protecting sensitive data, maintaining an audit trail and providing human oversight would cost more than the expected benefit, extending that particular pilot needs a stronger business case than the time and money already invested. - Brian Stimpfl, S-Docs.

In a recent development, end a pilot when the evidence invalidates its core business premise. If owners can complete the workflow but gain no meaningful time, cost or quality improvement over the current process, more engineering won’t create demand. Define that minimum benefit before launch, test it with real users, and stop when it remains out of reach. - Irina Shymko, Langate Software.

Recent findings suggest that end the pilot when the team cannot define a credible path from the experiment to a measurable business outcome. If success still depends on vague future improvements, heroic manual support or assumptions the pilot was supposed to validate, extending it usually just delays the decision. - Dhyey Mavani, Abridge.

According to recent reports, A pilot should end when the team cannot explain what new evidence another extension will produce. Every extra week should answer a specific open question about value, risk, adoption, cost or scale. Once the remaining time is only keeping the pilot alive, the experiment has already delivered its answer. - Sibasis Padhi, Walmart Inc.

I would end a pilot when it successfully completes individual tasks but repeatedly fails to deliver the full business outcome. Often, the underlying issue is the absence of a clear decision model for handling exceptions, approvals or unresolved work across teams. If nobody can authorize what happens next, scaling the technology only scales the problem. - Vamshi Noothi, Cisco.

Recent findings suggest that A pilot should be ended if nobody uses it unless someone reminds them. A pilot that only stays alive while its sponsor keeps pushing won’t survive production, and extending it just postpones that answer. Software nobody uses isn’t free; it still costs money to run, maintain and support. End it, write down what you learned about the problem, and put the team on something people actually want. - Jeremy Suriel, Kustomer.

It has been revealed that A clear sign to end a technology pilot is when no business owner is willing to take responsibility for implementation. Even if the technology performs well, success requires business ownership, accountability and commitment to change. Without a sponsor willing to champion the solution, allocate resources and own the outcomes, extending the pilot is unlikely to deliver value. Technology cannot create lasting benefits without clear business ownership. - Eranda Maldeniya, Enterprise Analytics.

Tech Report: College Scholarship Breakdown: Types, Sponsors and Eligibility at a Glance

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1371 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nerdwallet

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that scholarships have become a standard part of applying for college.
  • Before you go searching for a scholarship, it's important to understand the types of scholarships available and how to identify the ones that give you the best chance of winning, which can save you time and potentially earn you more funding.
  • Scholarships are often funded by three groups: private organizations, institutions like universities, and government agencies.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that scholarships have become a standard part of applying for college. You can learn about scholarships in a variety of ways, but looking through an online database of available scholarships — the most common way — can be overwhelming.

Before you go searching for a scholarship, it's important to understand the types of scholarships available and how to identify the ones that give you the best chance of winning, which can save you time and potentially earn you more funding. Here’s what you need to know about scholarships to decide which ones are best for you.

Scholarships are often funded by three groups: private organizations, institutions like universities, and government agencies. None is better than the other when it comes to awarding funds.

Nonprofit organizations and clubs that are looking for students either majoring in or researching certain fields, or who have experience volunteering in a specific field.

Companies that want to support all students or only fund those majoring in a field that relates to the companies’ industries.

Financial institutions, such as banks or credit unions, that want to support their community or their members.

Individuals or families that are funding private scholarships, usually in memory of a loved one.

Universities and colleges that are offering funds to students who attend their campuses.

Research organizations that want to fund students who will research in their areas of interest and further their causes.

These scholarships generally are provided by local, state or federal government agencies for a variety of reasons. Despite being funded by a government agency, the scholarships do not require you to pay back the money — unlike federal student loans.

Sources indicate that some scholarships pay for anything related to college expenses, including tuition, room and board, books and supplies, and more. Other scholarships limit what you can pay for with the funds, such as only tuition or tuition along with books. It’s important to look at this restriction when applying for scholarships to ensure the funds will go toward what you need to cover.

Merit scholarships require you to show excellence or achievements in your schoolwork, through talents and abilities, and even leadership or service work. Because these types of awards can be highly competitive, merit scholarships might require more than just achievements, such as volunteer or leadership experience. This means merit-based scholarships can overlap with other types of scholarship categories. Here are some examples of merit-based scholarships:.

Merit scholarships often require you to have earned a minimum grade point average (GPA). The minimum GPA depends on the scholarship but often ranges from 2.0 to 4.0, with more competitive scholarships usually requiring higher GPAs. Scholarships with lower GPA minimums are more likely to consider additional factors, such as financial need.

Some merit scholarships might require a minimum ACT or SAT score instead of a GPA — or in addition to a minimum GPA.

It has been revealed that merit scholarships might also require applicants to have participated in activities outside of their schoolwork. This is common for scholarships that require membership in a certain group or organization. For example, membership in agricultural clubs, such as 4-H or FFA, and scouting groups, such as the National Eagle Scout Association, appear in scholarship requirements.

Some scholarships emphasize volunteering or community service and only consider applicants who have that experience. Applications vary in how detailed their requirements can be. Some scholarships want only a general description of where and how you’ve volunteered, and others might require experience with a service project that indicates more leadership experience or time volunteering with a certain type of organization.

Scholarships that are awarded to students who can’t afford college are called need-based scholarships.

It has been revealed that unmet financial need is the difference between what it will cost you to attend college and what you can afford to pay. Because calculating how much you can afford is a complicated process, many scholarships refer to your FAFSA to document your financial need.

Some scholarship requirements may be as straightforward as demonstrating that you have financial need, but some scholarships might have income limits. However, income restrictions are less common.

Athletic scholarships are for — you guessed it — athletes. They are usually offered by colleges and universities to recruit athletes onto their collegiate teams and can be competitive. Which sports have scholarships available and the scholarship amounts vary by college.

Even though the main criterion for an athletic scholarship is being good at your sport, you’ll likely still need to show that you can keep up with your schoolwork. Most athletic scholarships require students to earn a minimum GPA or test scores to remain eligible while they’re in college.

In a recent development, some scholarships are designated for students majoring in a general field, such as science or education, but others can be for very specific areas of study. For example, a scholarship for students majoring in a natural resource field could include majors in biology, ecology, wildlife biology, conservation education, forestry, soils and hydrology. However, a stricter scholarship might state that students have to major in more specific topics, such as biochemistry or microbial ecology.

According to recent reports, scholarships are available for active and former members of the military and members of their families. In addition to federal funds available for veterans to attend college, private organizations and some universities have scholarships for veterans to offset the cost of a degree.

Which family members can apply for funds depends on the individual scholarship. For example, some scholarships extend to children or spouses of veterans, but some go as far in a family tree as great-grandchildren.

Veteran- and military-focused scholarships might require that applicants or their family members enlisted in a certain branch, served during a particular time or conflict, or meet a certain rank or status such as receiving disability. Scholarships might also require that the applicant be a wartime veteran or family member of a wartime veteran; not all veterans meet this status.

Recent findings suggest that scholarships are also awarded to people who identify with a certain group. Common examples of identity-based scholarships include those for people who have disabilities, belong to certain ethnic or religious groups, identify as LGBTQIA+ or are first-generation students. Some identity-based scholarships require applicants to meet several criteria, such as belonging to more than one identity group.

Outside of what would be considered standard DEI groups, there are scholarships for applicants who identify with less common groups, such as veganism, homelessness and model railroad builders.

The best scholarships for you depend on your situation. For example, if you are a skilled athlete with a good academic record, going for an athletic scholarship might give you the most funding. On the other hand, if you’re going to research a topic that isn’t common, looking for scholarships that support your research topic might be your best bet because competition could be lower.

Good tactics to figure out which scholarships are worth your time include:.

Think of the skills, talents, experience and identities that are unique to you. For example, being a child of a veteran immediately qualifies you for scholarships with fewer applicants than scholarships open to everyone. Likewise, if you embrace a certain ethnicity, identify with a specific group or have experience with a type of work, you might qualify for scholarships that appreciate and recognize those attributes more than the average scholarship.

In a recent development, apply if you think you're eligible. Don’t apply to just a few scholarships and hope you get them. Instead, apply for as many scholarships as you can and for which you’re eligible. This increases your chances of receiving funds. Even small scholarships can make a big impact when you add several of them together.

Industry observers note that understand how you can use the money. If you already have a scholarship that covers only books, applying for the same type of scholarship isn’t helpful if you don’t need the extra funds. Instead, look for scholarships that cover the costs you have remaining.

Not sure where to look? Our sister site Scholarships360.org provides students with vetted scholarship opportunities. That would be a good place to start.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that few businesses exemplify American business success more than Coca-Cola (KO +0.94%).
  • Recent findings suggest that over the last 12 months alone, shares have jumped by an impressive 35%, substantially outpacing the S&P 500's return of just 8% over the same time frame.
  • To understand Coca-Cola's appeal, it can pay to listen to the philosophy of one of its biggest backers, Warren Buffett.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Will Ebiefung – Nov 20, 2026 at 5:05PM EST.

10 stocks we like better than Coca-Cola ›.

Industry observers note that few businesses exemplify American business success more than Coca-Cola (KO +0.94%). Since its founding in the late 19th century, the multinational beverage maker has expanded globally to serve billions and become one of the world's most recognized brands. Investors have profited substantially along the way, and this indicates little sign of stopping.

Recent findings suggest that over the last 12 months alone, shares have jumped by an impressive 35%, substantially outpacing the S&P 500's return of just 8% over the same time frame. This is a big deal for a organization that is already large and mature. Let's dig deeper into the pros and cons of Coca-Cola to decide if the company still has millionaire-maker potential.

NYSE · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

To understand Coca-Cola's appeal, it can pay to listen to the philosophy of one of its biggest backers, Warren Buffett. His Berkshire Hathaway portfolio owns a whopping $38.4 billion worth of Coca-Cola stock, making it his third-largest bet behind American Express and Apple.

According to recent reports, buffett likes to invest in companies with simple and easy-to-understand business models that enjoy a strong economic moat. A moat is a competitive advantage that protects a tech giant's market share against competition and allows it to enjoy stable or elevated pricing power. Coca-Cola is arguably the quintessential example of this type of business.

You can walk into a convenience store or restaurant practically anywhere in the world and find Coca-Cola's flagship beverage Coke (or one of its many subbrands like Sprite, Fanta, and a variety of localized options).

The company's ubiquitous shelf space has created unparalleled habit creation among its consumers, which is something new rivals will struggle to disrupt, even if they manage to create better-tasting products. This advantage also makes Coca-Cola's sales remarkably recession-resistant. It has allowed the company to protect its margins amid soaring global inflation in raw materials like aluminum and sugar.

Coca-Cola's gross margins have hovered around 60%, despite the soaring prices for its products. This suggests the organization is passing on the vast majority of inflation to consumers, while protecting its own profitability.

KO Gross Profit Margin data by YCharts.

Coca-Cola isn't without some long-term challenges. The manufacturer is already a global brand name, and that means there is very little room for organic growth. Management will be increasingly tempted to rely on price increases to juice investor returns. While the company's gross margin of over 60% was easy to justify back when a 12-pack cost $4.00, it is much harder to stomach when prices have doubled, and more American families are struggling to make ends meet.

Soda prices have far exceeded the U.S. inflation rate, despite boasting a disproportionately middle- and lower-income consumer base. It's hard not to wonder if this situation is as sustainable as it may look on the surface.

Over the long term, there could be a generational shift away from brand-name soft drinks as people become more comfortable buying lower-cost store brands from major retailers like Walmart, which offers alternatives like Sam's Cola and Twist Up.

Coca-Cola's recent performance is impressive, and its strong moat can help set the company up for more market-beating growth over the long term. That stated, with a market cap of $422 billion (in a mature industry with relatively little room for organic growth), Coca-Cola's days of explosive millionaire-making growth are likely behind it. Shares are also somewhat expensive at a forward price-to-earnings (P/E) multiple of 28.

According to recent reports, investors who buy the stock now should look at it as a safer alternative to more speculative opportunities like generative AI. The manufacturer's dividend (at the moment boasting a yield of 2.21%) will likely represent a sizable percentage of its long-term returns.

By Reuben Gregg Brewer – Nov 20, 2026 at 5:15PM EST.

10 stocks we like better than Pfizer ›.

Sources indicate that pfizer (PFE -0.51%) faces a large patent cliff, and investors worry it won't be able to offset the revenue it loses as older drugs face generic competition. That's a problem, but the drugmaker is aware of it and is making crucial strides in its efforts to address the issue. The big story, however, is that this issue is pretty normal for a drug tech giant.

In fact, revenue from recently launched and acquired drugs rose 32% in the third quarter of 2026. That highlights the pharmaceutical giant's efforts are bearing fruit. But there's more reason to be excited, including the company's strong balance sheet, its large dividend, and management's commitment to continue paying that dividend. Here's what you need to know.

One of the biggest worries about Pfizer is its upcoming patent expirations. Two big ones are Eliquis in 2028 and Vyndamax in 2031. But patent expirations are a normal part of the pharma sector. And research and development efforts in the highly technical and intensely competitive healthcare sector don't always align perfectly with a company's patent expiration schedule. It's just a fact of life.

Industry observers note that the 32% revenue growth Pfizer achieved from launched and acquired products is evidence that the company is seeing some success in its efforts to address the matter. And it sets up three more reasons to consider buying the stock.

Pfizer ended the third quarter of 2026 with $1.8 billion in cash and $12.4 billion in short-term investments. That gives the company significant firepower to support its business through this patent-expiration cycle. In fact, the company's cash hoard is slightly higher than at the start of the year, so it isn't rapidly burning through its savings.

Sources indicate that despite the tech giant's results with new drugs and its financial strength, investors are deeply negative on Pfizer's stock. That's highlighted by its huge 6.1% dividend yield as of this writing. To put that yield into context, the S&P 500 index (^GSPC -3.70%) yields roughly 1.1%, and the average pharma stock yields 1.3%.

It has been revealed that the negativity highlighted by the elevated yield is echoed by more traditional valuation metrics. Pfizer's price-to-sales and price-to-book ratios are below their five-year averages. And while the price-to-earnings ratio is elevated, it is largely due to one-time charges. Looking at the whole picture, Pfizer's stock looks attractively priced.

NYSE · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

It has been revealed that given the lofty yield, Pfizer is likely to be most appealing to dividend-focused investors. But right now earnings aren't covering the dividend. That's not a great sign, but one-time charges are part of the issue. If you look at cash flow, the organization can still support the dividend. That's highlighted by a cash dividend payout ratio of roughly 85%. While a lower number would be better, there's still some room for adversity. And don't forget about the company's large cash pile.

According to recent reports, both of these facts help support management's strong backing of the dividend. Indeed, one of Pfizer's key capital priorities is to "maintain and grow our dividend." Obviously, the organization's priorities could change, but it wouldn't make a statement like that if the board of directors wasn't on board with protecting the dividend.

It has been revealed that at the end of the day, Pfizer is facing very real headwinds today. But it is an industry-leading company with a long history of success. If history is any guide, it will muddle through this difficult period. The success it is having with upcoming drugs, its financial strength, attractive valuation, and dedication to its large dividend are all strong reasons for investors to take a deep dive before 2026 is over. If you wait too long, the opportunity here may pass you by.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Sara Appino – Updated Nov 20, 2026 at 5:29PM EST.

10 stocks we like better than BigBear.ai ›.

Choosing between these specialized AI plays requires balancing high-stakes government work against commercial data engineering growth. Investors must decide if BigBear.ai (BBAI -8.67%) or Innodata (INOD -8.91%) better suits their portfolio needs.

BigBear.ai provides complex decision intelligence tools for federal and defense agencies, while Innodata helps major tech firms train generative AI systems. Both companies operate in the rapidly evolving world of artificial intelligence but serve different markets. This comparison examines their financial health, customer concentration, and valuation to help you decide which stock fits your strategy.

According to recent reports, bigBear.ai offers decision intelligence solutions that combine data from different sources to help leaders make faster choices. It serves critical sectors like national security, cybersecurity, and global supply chains. According to its latest annual report, a specific contract accounted for nearly 51% of consolidated revenue. Customer concentration like this adds a layer of risk to the business.

In the 12 months ended Sept. 30, 2026, revenue reached nearly $142.1 million. This represented a revenue growth decline of approximately 1.5% compared to the prior period. The company reported a net loss of roughly $180.2 million during this same time frame.

Following its early 2026 debt conversion, the debt-to-equity ratio is approximately 0.0x, meaning the firm carries virtually no debt relative to its equity. The current ratio, which measures the ability to pay short-term debts with short-term assets, is close to 1.8x. In the fiscal year ended Dec. 31, 2025, free cash flow was negative at nearly $46.3 million.

In a recent development, innodata operates as a global data engineering firm that prepares and evaluates data for large-scale AI systems. The company serves several high-profile technology leaders, with one customer in its digital data solutions segment accounting for nearly 58% of total revenue in 2025. This focus on the best small cap tech stocks in the data sector highlights its role in the generative AI boom.

In the 12 months ended Sept. 30, 2026, revenue reached approximately $350.2 million. This reflects a revenue growth increase of nearly 46.9% over the previous year. The firm also achieved a net income of roughly $48.5 million during this period.

Industry observers note that as of its December 2025 balance sheet, the current ratio is approximately 2.7x. The debt-to-equity ratio is 0.0x, indicating a strong balance sheet with no total debt. In the fiscal year ended Dec. 31, 2025, free cash flow was nearly $35.6 million. Note that stock-based compensation represented roughly 23.8% of operating cash flow, which inflates reported cash generation since SBC is a non-cash expense added back in the cash flow statement.

BigBear.ai faces significant risk due to heavy revenue concentration with government customers who can terminate contracts for convenience. Scaling its sales efforts remains a challenge while managing long and unpredictable sales cycles. It also faces intense competition from Microsoft (MSFT -2.77%) and Amazon (AMZN -4.10%). The company also navigates complex AI deployment risks and recent financial volatility including litigation over accounting errors.

Innodata relies heavily on a single customer that contributed nearly 58% of its 2025 revenues, making it vulnerable to contract changes. It competes against well-resourced firms like Accenture (ACN +1.19%) and Cognizant Technology Solutions (CTSH +3.11%) in the data engineering space. The business also deals with geopolitical risks from its global workforce and ongoing legal challenges regarding securities class actions.

Innodata appears to offer a more attractive value proposition based on its lower P/S ratio, which measures market value against sales over the past twelve months.

Valuation metrics include sourcing from Financial Modeling Prep (FMP) and may differ from other data providers.

I'd go with Innodata. AI models are only as good as the data they learn from, and Innodata helps significant tech companies create and test that data. Its sales have grown year over year for 13 straight quarters, and it makes money.

It has been revealed that last quarter, sales jumped 53% and management raised its growth outlook, though the stock has fallen sharply this fall. There are risks: Two customers make up most of its sales, margins narrowed, and one program is winding down. But Innodata is adding latest customers and work from a large cloud company, and expects to replace the lost program by early next year.

To give BigBear.ai its due, it does high-stakes work for national security and border security customers with contracts that are difficult to replace, and its backlog is growing. But it's still losing money, and government contract sales can be difficult to predict. That uncertainty is where Innodata stands apart: It is already profitable, with plenty of cash to keep investing as demand for AI data grows.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Arizona Cardinals might be turning to their fourth quarterback of the season.

In a press conference, Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur mentioned Carson Beck is dealing with back spasms and did not practice Friday. As a result, the team is preparing for backup Josh Johnson to be the team's starting quarterback for Week 11.

"Not gonna shut the door on him [Beck], but we're gonna proceed as if Josh is gonna be starting on Sunday," LaFleur stated.

In a recent development, beck, who is a rookie, was thrust into the role of starter after Gardner Minshew went on injured reserve with a torn UCL. The Cardinals' original starter, Jacoby Brissett, was traded to the Baltimore Ravens after being benched for Minshew mid-game the week before.

Beck was officially ruled as questionable in Friday's injury report.

According to recent reports, laFleur mentioned in his press conference that the team will monitor how Beck responds to treatment and how he feels on Saturday before making any final decisions. The coach added that this is an issue that Beck has dealt with before, but wasn't able to provide a clear timeline for Beck's return.

In the meantime, Johnson, who was signed off the Cincinnati Bengals' practice squad after the Minshew injury, looks poised to be stepping up for Sunday's matchup against the Kansas City Chiefs.

The itinerant backup quarterback also has some history with LaFleur: Johnson and LaFleur's careers overlapped in 2021, when both were with the New York Jets (LaFleur was an offensive coordinator at the time). LaFleur had high praise for Johnson, noting some of the reasons he's been able to keep his career going this long.

"If it is Josh, I've called plays for him before, and had a really great experience calling plays for him," LaFleur remarked. "He is incredible in the quarterback room, he's incredible for the starters. He's incredible for young quarterbacks, in terms of the way he sees the game, his energy, his positivity, how he keeps it real. He's mature. And he can still sling it. … If that's the route that ends up happening, let's go.".

Arizona is the 15th NFL franchise that Johnson has been a part of in his career, as the 40-year-old quarterback has bounced between half of the teams in the league. Across 16 seasons, he has only started 11 games in his NFL career.

Here's the Average Social Security Benefit at Age 67

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (667 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fool

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Kailey Hagen, CFP® – Nov 20, 2026 at 6:00PM EST.
  • It has been revealed that the average Social Security benefit for 67-year-olds is $2,016.48 per month, according to Social Security Administration (SSA) data from December 2025.
  • According to recent reports, reaching this age doesn't always mean you receive exactly 100% of your baseline amount.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Kailey Hagen, CFP® – Nov 20, 2026 at 6:00PM EST.

It has been revealed that the average Social Security benefit for 67-year-olds is $2,016.48 per month, according to Social Security Administration (SSA) data from December 2025. Full retirement age (FRA) ranges from 66 to 67, depending on your birth year, and it's 67 for everyone born in 1960 or later. It's the point where you're eligible for your unreduced retirement amount.

According to recent reports, reaching this age doesn't always mean you receive exactly 100% of your baseline amount. Many people who are 67 today have a full retirement age of 66 years and 10 months. These workers may have already earned small delayed retirement credits if they waited until 67 to claim their checks.

Industry observers note that earnings histories also impact these averages. Men who are 67 receive an average of $2,234.41 per month, while the average among women is $1,801.82. This results in a monthly gender gap of $432.59 as of December 2025.

Recent findings suggest that think of your full retirement age as the baseline for your benefits. The SSA bases your check on your average monthly income over your 35 highest-earning years, adjusting those wages for inflation and applying the primary insurance amount formula. This calculation creates the standard amount you're entitled to at full retirement age.

You don't have to claim at your baseline. You can earn delayed retirement credits, which are increases for delaying past FRA, worth 8% per year up to age 70. For a worker whose FRA is 67, waiting those three extra years provides a 24% total increase in monthly income.

Recent findings suggest that these decisions have a visible impact on the data. The average monthly benefit at age 70 is $2,274.68, which is $258.20 higher than the age-67 average.

Recent findings suggest that but even for these claimants, benefits alone often aren't enough to live on. Social Security was only designed to replace about 40% of pre-retirement wages, so most retirees rely on savings or other income to cover their full costs.

A 3.6% cost-of-living adjustment (COLA) will take effect in 2027 to help benefits keep pace with inflation. This will add about $73 a month on top of the average listed above. These adjustments are designed to protect your purchasing power over time.

Knowing the population average gives you a target for your own planning, but your final check depends on your career earnings and when you choose to claim.

Waiting until age 67 to claim Social Security helps you avoid the early claiming benefit reduction, which can drastically reduce your checks. This is one major reason FRA is such a popular claiming age, but it's not the only one.

It has been revealed that when you claim Social Security under your FRA, you're also at risk of losing some of your benefits to the earnings test if you're still working. In 2027, for example, you lose $1 from your checks for every $2 you earn over $25,960 if you're under your FRA all year. If you'll reach your FRA next year, you only lose $1 for every $3 you earn over $67,920.

In a recent development, these lost benefits come back to you as a permanent benefit boost at your FRA. But for some, the risk of short-term losses makes them delay their claim until their FRA, when the earnings test no longer applies. This is something to weigh if you blueprint to continue working once you're eligible for Social Security checks.

    PayPal vs. SoFi Technologies: Which Financial Stock Is a Better Buy for 2027?

    📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (929 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fool

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • By Sara Appino – Updated Nov 20, 2026 at 6:05PM EST.
    • Deciding between PayPal (PYPL -5.46%) and SoFi Technologies (SOFI -7.76%) requires balancing established market dominance against aggressive digital growth.
    • Industry observers note that payPal remains a global giant in payment processing, while SoFi is a fast-growing digital bank targeting a younger, high-earning demographic.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Sara Appino – Updated Nov 20, 2026 at 6:05PM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than PayPal ›.

    Deciding between PayPal (PYPL -5.46%) and SoFi Technologies (SOFI -7.76%) requires balancing established market dominance against aggressive digital growth. Both companies are fighting for a larger share of your digital wallet today.

    Industry observers note that payPal remains a global giant in payment processing, while SoFi is a fast-growing digital bank targeting a younger, high-earning demographic. While they operate in different niches, both compete for the same pool of consumer financial activity, making them frequent candidates for a fintech-focused portfolio as investors look toward the future of money.

    Industry observers note that payPal operates a massive digital payments platform serving nearly 439 million active accounts across 200 markets. It provides branded checkout services, person-to-person payments via Venmo, and even Bitcoin (CRYPTO:BTC) trading within its app. This scale makes it one of the most recognizable names in fintech stocks today as it adapts to a changing financial landscape.

    In a recent development, reliable recent quarterly figures for at least one of these companies aren't available, so this comparison uses each company's latest full fiscal year. For FY 2025, PayPal reported revenue of nearly $33.2 billion, representing growth of approximately 4.3% over the prior year. The company generated net income of close to $5.2 billion, showing a steady ability to convert its high volume of transactions into profit for its shareholders.

    As of its December 2025 balance sheet, the debt-to-equity ratio reached roughly 0.5x, comparing total debt to shareholder equity. The current ratio, which compares short-term assets to short-term liabilities, was approximately 1.3x. Free cash flow, or the cash remaining after paying for operations and equipment, was nearly $5.6 billion in FY 2025.

    SoFi Technologies is a mobile-first financial services provider that offers a wide range of products including student loan refinancing, home loans, and investment tools. It serves approximately 15.8 million members and has expanded into business services through a partnership with Mastercard (MA -0.14%). The firm also supports Bitcoin trading and provides modern banking infrastructure to other firms through its proprietary technology segments.

    In a recent development, for its latest annual report covering FY 2025, SoFi Technologies generated revenue of nearly $3.6 billion, which was an increase of approximately 35.1% compared to the previous year. The firm reported net income of close to $481.3 million, marking a significant transition into consistent profitability. This growth was driven by a diversified mix of lending products and financial services that attracted latest members to its platform.

    Sources indicate that based on its December 2025 balance sheet, the debt-to-equity ratio was roughly 0.2x, helping investors see the low level of debt relative to shareholder equity. The current ratio was approximately 0.2x, which measures a company's ability to cover immediate liabilities with assets that can be quickly converted to cash. Free cash flow for the year was a net loss of nearly $4.0 billion, which often occurs in banking as capital is deployed into upcoming loans rather than held as cash.

    PayPal faces intense competition from both traditional banks and newer technology platforms that offer digital checkout solutions. The company is also subject to extensive global regulatory oversight regarding payment processing and anti-money laundering rules. Any failure to manage cybersecurity risks or protect user data could lead to significant penalties and damage its reputation.

    SoFi Technologies must manage the complex regulatory requirements that come with being a bank holding organization. It relies on a concentrated number of whole loan purchasers, meaning its results could suffer if these buyers reduce their activity. Additionally, the company faces the challenge of managing rapid growth across its various lending and technology segments without increasing credit risks.

    When comparing these two companies using Forward P/E, PayPal looks significantly cheaper than its peer based on future earnings estimates.

    Valuation metrics include sourcing from Financial Modeling Prep (FMP) and may differ from other data providers.

    I'd go with SoFi Technologies. Its sales and earnings are both growing far faster than PayPal's, and it has built a full digital bank with more than 17 million members, starting from student loans. Its bank charter lets it fund loans with its members' deposits, a cost advantage most fintech rivals lack.

    Sources indicate that soFi also gave investors its 2027 outlook a full quarter early, and it came in above analysts' expectations, with revenue expected to grow about 27%. Management built it assuming interest rates keep rising, even after a rate hike this year hurt the stock. The shares are still down for the year, so long-term investors get a lower price for a profitable, growing business.

    In a recent development, to give PayPal its due, it is a household name that produces plenty of cash, and Venmo is growing fast. But its original business, letting shoppers pay online with their PayPal account, is barely growing, and overall sales are rising slowly. By contrast, SoFi's lending and banking businesses are surging, and even its technology business, which lost a large client, is expected to return to growth in 2027. For long-term investors, that mix of growth, profits, and a lower price makes SoFi the better buy for 2027.
