    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Plenty of companies are growing incredibly well right now, including several from the artificial intelligence business.
    • Except for orbital launch and satellite tech specialist Rocket Lab (RKLB -10.92%), it isn't.
    • Rocket Lab offers satellite launch solutions.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By James Brumley – Nov 20, 2026 at 6:30PM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Rocket Lab ›.

    Plenty of companies are growing incredibly well right now, including several from the artificial intelligence business. A tech giant that's set to triple its top line over the course of the next couple of years, though? That seems outrageous.

    Except for orbital launch and satellite tech specialist Rocket Lab (RKLB -10.92%), it isn't. This future business is already lined up. These paying customers are just waiting for one pivotal milestone that's likely to materialize sometime next year. Then the floodgates open.

    Rocket Lab offers satellite launch solutions. Its relatively small Electron rocket design has now been debuted 100 times, putting 273 satellites into low earth orbit.

    In a recent development, the organization also provides a range of satellite components and construction services, which accounts for more than half of last quarter's revenue of $268 million. Rocket Lab expects to do around $980 billion in business in fiscal 2026, well up from last year's $602 billion.

    Industry observers note that this is just a taste of what's to come, though. As the organization confirmed with its third-quarter report posted earlier this month, Rocket Lab's backlog grew 52% from Q2's $2.36 billion to an incredible $3.6 billion. The organization just needs more capacity, but that's coming. Rocket Lab can now manufacture an Electron rocket every eight days.

    Then there's the proverbial 800-pound gorilla in the room. That's the company's larger Neutron rocket, which has seen its inaugural flight pushed back several times, with the first flight now expected sometime in 2027.

    It has been revealed that despite the delays so far, once Neutron is flying, everything takes a turn for the better. As CFO Adam Spice commented during the third-quarter's earnings conference call, adjusted earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortization (EBITDA) "will turn positive within six months of that first successful test flight," with cash flow likely to turn positive shortly after that.

    Sources indicate that neutron isn't the big profit center in and of itself, to be clear. It's just a means to an end. Being able to put larger, heavier satellites into orbit also opens up its satellite tech business. Of its newly introduced backlog of $3.6 billion, $1.7 billion of it reflects space systems rather than launch services, up 194% year over year.

    Sources indicate that to this end, while analysts aren't yet looking for Rocket Lab's revenue to triple between now and 2028, with recent failures of similar rockets like ULA's Vulcan and one earlier in the year from Blue Origin, Rocket Lab is promptly becoming a preferred launch option. It may well exceed 2028's expectations.

    It has been revealed that as for the impact on the stock, it's not a complicated prediction to make. If the manufacturer's top line comes anywhere close to tripling by 2028, the bullish argument firms up enormously.

    While it may not triple in value in step with revenue, $3 billion in sales could turn this high-growth $34 billion outfit into a $60 billion outfit with relative ease. And given that the tech giant isn't likely to raise money by issuing more stock anytime soon, that translates into a near-doubling of the stock's price.

    NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

    You're getting some help in the meantime, by the way. The analyst community overwhelmingly considers RKLB stock a strong buy right now, with a 12-month consensus price target of $93.30 already more than 80% above the ticker's current price.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • In a recent development, september ended on a mixed note, with the S&P 500 and Dow Jones Industrial Average falling 0.5% and 4.3%, respectively, while the Nasdaq Composite climbed 1.9%.
    • In this climate, investors with a long-term horizon can track recommendations from top Wall Street analysts to find stocks with solid growth prospects.
    • Here are three stocks favored by some of Wall Street's top pros, according to TipRanks, a platform that ranks analysts based on their past performance.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    In a recent development, september ended on a mixed note, with the S&P 500 and Dow Jones Industrial Average falling 0.5% and 4.3%, respectively, while the Nasdaq Composite climbed 1.9%. Markets remained on edge with higher oil prices and Treasury yields weighing on investor sentiment and triggering fears of additional interest rate hikes.

    In this climate, investors with a long-term horizon can track recommendations from top Wall Street analysts to find stocks with solid growth prospects.

    Here are three stocks favored by some of Wall Street's top pros, according to TipRanks, a platform that ranks analysts based on their past performance.

    Neocloud tech giant CoreWeave (CRWV) is benefiting from robust AI-driven demand for cloud computing.

    Recently, JPMorgan analyst Samik Chatterjee upgraded CoreWeave to buy from hold, raising his price target to $125 from $120. The analyst cited favorable pricing, driven by solid demand, for the upgrade.

    Sources indicate that chatterjee said CoreWeave is now more willing to sign premium priced, shorter-term contracts, which lift his revenue and margin estimates. CRWV stock performance has been underwhelming as investors worry about high capital spending, the analyst noted. That said, he believes that higher prices and increased margins will more than offset the rise in debt to fund capital spending, improving the stock's valuation.

    Chatterjee noted the 25% price hike in July across CoreWeave's product offerings and frequent price increases by rivals like Nebius (NBIS), adding that some peers are charging nearly three times more for short-term compute contracts than what CoreWeave charges on longer-term deals.

    "CoreWeave's leverage of the opportunity [is] evident in its recent press release highlighting contracts signed in F3Q at ~$40M/MW," mentioned Chatterjee. JPMorgan said higher pricing is already contributing 5-10 percentage points to contract margins versus earlier deals.

    In a recent development, chatterjee ranks No. 4 among more than 12,500 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been successful 75% of the time, delivering an average return of 55.3%. See CoreWeave Statistics on TipRanks.

    Palo Alto Networks (PANW) is a provider of cybersecurity solutions across network, cloud, security operations, AI and identity. Following a discussion with management, BTIG analyst Gray Powell reiterated a buy rating on PANW and raised his price target to $425 from $404.

    After a review of Palo Alto's product-level growth catalysts, Powell sees clear upside to both revenue and next-generation security (NGS) annual recurring revenue (ARR) in fiscal 2027. He expects PANW to deliver pro forma revenue growth of more than 17%, above the consensus estimate of 14.6%, and NGS ARR growth of more than 26% versus the Street's expectation of 24.5%.

    It has been revealed that over the past five years, the Palo Alto business mix, has moved to higher-growth product areas and fresh markets. from what was earlier viewed as a hardware-centric network security company, Powell stated. The 5-star analyst estimates that hardware firewalls and attached subscriptions now account for less than 50% of revenue.

    According to recent reports, meanwhile, high-growth solutions, including Prisma SASE, software firewalls, Cortex XSIAM, Chronosphere and Idira now represent more than 35% of PANW's revenue. "Investors may not fully realize the growth potential within PANW's platform story," Powell mentioned.

    BTIG is optimistic about the prospects of Chronosphere in observability, CyberArk in identity and software firewalls and Prisma AIRS in the network and AI security business.

    Powell ranks No. 320 among more than 12,500 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been profitable 61% of the time, delivering an average return of 17.3%. See Palo Alto Networks KPIs on TipRanks.

    In a research note on September 30, Rosenblatt analyst Scott Devitt reiterated a buy rating on e-commerce and cloud computing platform Amazon (AMZN), raising his price target to $360 from $335. Fears that agentic commerce poses a major threat to Amazon's advertising business seem "overstated," he noted.

    Recent findings suggest that devitt noted that the growing adoption of personal agents and AI shopping assistants has sparked concern about displacement of Amazon's retail media business. But the 5-star analyst remains bullish, given Amazon's ability to adapt to changing consumer behavior, as it's done in the past.

    Additionally, Devitt argues that even if an AI agent helps a shopper discover a product, Amazon can still handle the purchase and delivery, keeping much of the transaction value. He highlighted that management believes that existing Amazon shoppers will likely continue to start their shopping journey on the platform because it has better personalization, accurate pricing and inventory information that third-party agents still lack.

    It has been revealed that overall, Devitt expects Amazon's retail business to prove a net beneficiary of agentic commerce. Fewer clicks would not hurt the company if the value of each remaining click and overall volumes keep rising, he noted. The argument is that even if Amazon loses some sponsored ad revenue over the next few years, it would likely be only a small part of the company's total business and could be offset by growth in other areas.

    It has been revealed that "Consistent with our AI framework, we continue to view Amazon as one of the most resilient leaders in our coverage, combining owned compute infrastructure with a physical fulfillment moat," said Devitt. His bullish view is supported, Devitt said, by expectations that Amazon Web Services (AWS) will exit the year at a more than 45% growth rate with continued margin improvement.

    Sources indicate that devitt ranks No. 765 among more than 12,500 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been profitable 49% of the time, delivering an average return of 12%. See Amazon Ownership Structure on TipRanks.

    Prediction: Nvidia Stock Will Do This in the 6 Months After a Newly introduced CEO Takes Over, According to History

    📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (878 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fool

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Nvidia (NVDA -14.01%) is navigating one of the most consequential leadership transitions in recent Silicon Valley history.
    • Colette Kress, Nvidia's former chief financial officer, is now serving as interim CEO while the board searches for a permanent successor.
    • Recent findings suggest that history offers some clues about how technology stocks behave following major CEO transitions.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Adam Spatacco – Nov 20, 2026 at 6:42PM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Nvidia ›.

    Nvidia (NVDA -14.01%) is navigating one of the most consequential leadership transitions in recent Silicon Valley history. Following founder Jensen Huang's unexpected resignation amid a controversy involving alleged connections to Chinese intelligence, investors are growing increasingly concerned about the manufacturer's future. This uncertainty is weighing heavily on Nvidia stock, even as its underlying business continues to deliver extraordinary financial results.

    Colette Kress, Nvidia's former chief financial officer, is now serving as interim CEO while the board searches for a permanent successor. According to reports, the tech giant is considering external candidates, including Arm Holdings CEO Rene Haas.

    Recent findings suggest that history offers some clues about how technology stocks behave following major CEO transitions. However, Nvidia's circumstances are quite different from those of its peers, making the manufacturer's financial outlook particularly crucial right now.

    Microsoft (MSFT -2.77%) represents a successful example of a technology leadership transition. Satya Nadella became CEO on Feb. 4, 2014, replacing Steve Ballmer after Microsoft conducted a formal succession search. Nadella had previously led Microsoft's cloud and enterprise businesses, giving him extensive knowledge of the firm's operations.

    Microsoft stock advanced roughly 19% during Nadella's first six months as CEO. Of course, over the long term, he helped transform the Windows developer into a cloud computing powerhouse.

    Sources indicate that alphabet (GOOGL -2.70%) (GOOG -2.59%) offers another example. Sundar Pichai became CEO of Alphabet on Dec. 3, 2019, succeeding co-founder Larry Page. However, Pichai had already served as Google's CEO since 2015, making the transition more of a consolidation of leadership responsibilities than an unexpected management overhaul.

    Alphabet stock was higher roughly six months later, despite experiencing a meaningful drawdown during the short-lived COVID-19 market crash. Moreover, Page and his co-founder Sergey Brin remained involved as shareholders and directors, providing continuity that Nvidia currently lacks.

    Industry observers note that amazon (AMZN -4.10%) experienced a different outcome when Andy Jassy succeeded Jeff Bezos on July 5, 2021. Jassy was another internal executive who had previously built and led Amazon Web Services (AWS). Although Bezos relinquished the CEO position, he remains executive chairman, preserving his influence over the firm's long-term strategy.

    It has been revealed that amazon shares declined approximately 6% during Jassy's first six months as CEO. At the time, investors were assessing the impacts of slowing pandemic-era growth and rising operating expenses on Amazon's e-commerce marketplace.

    The three examples above show that CEO succession can bring different short-term outcomes. However, they also share an vital characteristic: Each of these companies promoted an experienced internal executive through an orderly transition, unlike Nvidia's abrupt leadership disruption.

    Nvidia's situation is unusual because Huang wasn't just another corporate executive. He co-founded Nvidia in 1993 and spent more than three decades directing the tech giant's evolution from a graphics chip manufacturer into the world's leading supplier of artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure. His influence extended across engineering, product development, corporate culture, and customer relationships.

    As a result of his departure, investors are increasingly questioning whether Nvidia can maintain its technological edge without the executive who helped establish it. The uncertainty is compounded by growing competition from custom AI accelerators developed by Alphabet, Amazon, and other hyperscalers. Nvidia's next CEO needs to prove they can preserve the manufacturer's innovation-driven culture while navigating complicated supply chains and regulatory relationships.

    NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

    Despite the unusual circumstances, Nvidia's financial outlook provides a compelling reason to anticipate a meaningful recovery. During its fiscal third-quarter earnings call, management increased its fiscal 2028 revenue growth forecast to 75%, up from its previous outlook of 70%. This suggests demand for Nvidia's accelerated computing platforms remains strong despite Huang's departure.

    Furthermore, Nvidia expects to generate $130 billion in revenue during the fourth quarter -- representing 91% growth year over year. The tech giant is also forecasting gross margins of between 72% and 73% in fiscal 2028, suggesting that accelerating sales growth will translate into additional profits.

    In a recent development, nvidia's share repurchase program provides another subtle catalyst for the stock. In September, the board increased the company's existing authorization by $150 billion, leaving approximately $227.3 billion available at the end of the third quarter. Management intends to execute the remaining authorization by the end of fiscal 2028.

    By reducing the number of outstanding shares, stock buybacks can increase earnings per share (EPS) even if net income is unchanged. Combined with Nvidia's revenue growth and profit margins, upcoming share repurchases should fuel substantial EPS expansion over the coming year.

    According to recent reports, my prediction is that Nvidia stock will trade higher six months after its new CEO assumes the role. The appointment itself should remove the primary source of uncertainty around the manufacturer, allowing investors to concentrate once again on revenue growth, earnings power, and competitive advantages.

    Here's How Much Nvidia Stock Is Worth Without Jensen Huang, According to Dan Ives

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Nvidia (NVDA -14.01%) has experienced a stunning reversal following founder Jensen Huang's unexpected resignation amid controversy surrounding alleged connections to Chinese intelligence.
    • In a recent development, the magnitude of the decline is anything but trivial.
    • Nevertheless, Wall Street analyst Dan Ives thinks investors are overlooking Nvidia's underlying earnings power.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Adam Spatacco – Nov 20, 2026 at 7:10PM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Nvidia ›.

    Nvidia (NVDA -14.01%) has experienced a stunning reversal following founder Jensen Huang's unexpected resignation amid controversy surrounding alleged connections to Chinese intelligence. Investors are increasingly questioning whether the semiconductor behemoth can maintain its technological edge without the executive who spent more than three decades building the firm. Those concerns have contributed to a dramatic sell-off, even as Nvidia continues reporting ridiculously good financial results.

    In a recent development, the magnitude of the decline is anything but trivial. Nvidia stock reached a record closing price of around $239 in early October but has fallen to roughly $136 as of Nov. 20. That represents a decline of roughly 43%, wiping out more than $2.5 trillion in market capitalization and pushing Nvidia from the world's most valuable public tech giant to fourth place.

    NVDA Market Cap data by YCharts.

    Nevertheless, Wall Street analyst Dan Ives thinks investors are overlooking Nvidia's underlying earnings power. Although he acknowledges that Huang's departure changes the organization's investment thesis, his revised price target suggests meaningful upside remains.

    Ives has been particularly vocal about the consequences of Huang's resignation. During a recent interview, he estimated that Huang contributed $1 trillion to Nvidia's valuation. In a separate appearance, Ives described Huang as the tech giant's "heart and lungs," emphasizing his influence over Nvidia's technological roadmap and competitive position.

    Ives claims Nvidia stock is worth $225 without Huang and $300 with him as CEO. These figures provide an interesting way to quantify the so-called Jensen premium. The difference between Ives' two valuations is $75 per share, representing a 25% reduction from his original $300 target.

    In a recent development, the implied difference in market capitalization is actually considerably larger than the $1 trillion Ives alluded to. With approximately 24.2 billion shares outstanding, a $75 difference translates into roughly $1.8 trillion in equity value. At Ives' respective price targets, Nvidia would command a market capitalization of approximately $7.3 trillion with Huang and $5.4 trillion without him.

    The difference in valuation illustrates the enormous importance Wall Street places on Nvidia's founder and why investors have reacted so negatively to his departure.

    Dan Ives. Image source: Getty Images.

    Huang's value extends beyond his responsibilities as CEO. Since co-founding Nvidia in 1993, he has overseen the company's transformation from a graphics processing company into the dominant supplier of accelerated computing infrastructure. His investments in GPUs, CUDA software, and AI computing helped position Nvidia at the center of the technology industry's most vital transformation since the birth of the internet.

    Perhaps Huang's greatest contribution has been leading Nvidia's culture of innovation. Huang consistently anticipated computing trends years before they became commercially relevant. This enabled Nvidia to develop new chip architectures and software ecosystems that competitors have struggled to replicate. This foresight helps establish durable competitive advantages and contributes to the company's pricing power.

    Huang also cultivated relationships with other technology executives, hyperscalers, governments, and AI labs. These supply chain connections have become important as Nvidia participates in data center build-outs that require complex financing arrangements and long-term strategic commitments.

    With all of that remarked, Nvidia's competitive advantages are not going to disappear just because Huang stepped away. The firm's hardware and software ecosystem, engineering workforce, customer relationships, and product roadmap remain intact.

    In a recent development, moreover, Ives acknowledges that Nvidia has a lead of two to three years over its competitors in AI chip technology. Although Huang's departure could narrow that advantage over time, the company's existing leadership provides a robust foundation for future growth.

    Recent findings suggest that jensen Huang. Image source: Getty Images.

    According to recent reports, despite reducing his Nvidia price target from $300 to $225, Ives maintains a bullish outlook on the company. At approximately $136 per share, his revised target implies roughly 65% upside, while his original $300 estimate implies 121% potential appreciation.

    NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

    Recent findings suggest that importantly, Ives' optimism centers on the insatiable demand for AI computing infrastructure and Nvidia's technological advantages. Following the company's earnings report on Nov. 17, Ives wrote that the results answered a critical question: "Demand did not leave with him.".

    The financial evidence supports that assessment. Nvidia generated $115.8 billion in fiscal third-quarter revenue, representing 103% growth year over year, while data center revenue surged 110% to $107.6 billion. The manufacturer also reported a gross margin of 74.8%, demonstrating that its pricing power remains strong.

    It has been revealed that furthermore, Nvidia forecast $130 billion in revenue for the fourth quarter and raised its fiscal 2028 revenue growth outlook to 75%. This forecast suggests the tech giant is poised for further expansion despite the leadership transition.

    Industry observers note that the central takeaway from Ives' analysis is that Nvidia doesn't necessarily need Huang to remain an attractive investment. Although his departure has reduced -- for now -- the premium investors are willing to pay, his price target still suggests considerable appreciation over the coming year. For investors who can stomach short-term volatility, Nvidia's recent sell-off could represent an opportunity to buy the dip in the most dominant AI infrastructure business at a significantly discounted valuation.

    Bristol Myers Squibb's Growth Portfolio Just Hit $7.7 Billion. Is This Cheap Pharma Stock a No-Brainer Buy?

    📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (699 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fool

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • By Reuben Gregg Brewer – Nov 20, 2026 at 7:15PM EST.
    • 10 stocks we like better than Bristol Myers Squibb ›.
    • Bristol Myers Squibb (BMY +0.79%) is a large, well-respected pharmaceutical tech giant.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Reuben Gregg Brewer – Nov 20, 2026 at 7:15PM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Bristol Myers Squibb ›.

    Bristol Myers Squibb (BMY +0.79%) is a large, well-respected pharmaceutical tech giant. It traces its history back to the mid-1800s. Right now, the company's portfolio of newer drugs, which it calls its "growth portfolio", just generated nearly $7.7 billion in revenue in a single quarter. That's a 12% increase over the same quarter in 2025. But is the stock worth buying? The risk/reward balance looks tilted toward reward for all but the most conservative investors. Here's why.

    The success Bristol Myers Squibb is having with its growth portfolio clearly indicates that this pharmaceutical giant hasn't lost its mojo. But investors are still downbeat on the stock (more on this below). So the dividend yield is a lofty 4.3%. The S&P 500 index (^GSPC -3.70%) yields roughly 1.1%, the average healthcare stock yields 1.3%, and the average drug stock yields 1.3%. That above-market and industry yield will likely be very enticing to long-term dividend investors. Meanwhile, the roughly 55% dividend payout ratio leaves ample room for adversity and should mollify all but the most conservative income lovers.

    It has been revealed that notably, the dividend has been increased regularly, though not annually, for over three decades. There have been no dividend cuts along the way despite the manufacturer working through some difficult periods during that span. That indicates the board of directors is strongly committed to returning value to shareholders through a reliable, slowly growing dividend. Adding to the allure is the fact that the stock's 13x price-to-earnings ratio is notably below the pharma industry average of roughly 28x. The high yield and relatively low P/E ratio will likely be of interest to value investors.

    Sources indicate that growth investors will appreciate the above-highlighted success of the company's growth portfolio. That portfolio is a collection of over a dozen latest drugs that, as of the third quarter, account for nearly 60% of the company's drug revenues. That's good news and bad news, however, and it highlights the risk that investors face if they decide to buy Bristol Myers Squibb.

    The healthcare giant's legacy portfolio still accounts for around 40% of revenues, or roughly $5.4 billion. And one drug, Eliquis, is responsible for nearly $4.7 billion of that total. Eliquis is set to see generic competition as soon as 2028. When that happens, the revenue this drug produces will likely start to fall, and perhaps sharply. That is why investors remain downbeat on Bristol Myers Squibb's stock despite the success of its growth portfolio.

    NYSE · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

    It has been revealed that it is reasonable that extremely conservative investors might want to stay on the sidelines until after Eliquis' patent expires. However, it is important to remember that patent expirations are just a normal part of the pharmaceutical business. And given the success of the growth portfolio, Bristol Myers Squibb continues to execute well in new drug development. There's just a mismatch between when patents expire, which happens on a set schedule, and its development efforts, which do not happen on a set schedule.

    In order to buy Bristol Myers Squibb, you need to believe it will get through this period. History suggests it will, and that's backed up by the success of the growth portfolio.

    If you can't handle the uncertainty around the patent expiration of Eliquis, you shouldn't buy Bristol Myers Squibb. However, for most investors, including dividend, value, and perhaps even growth-focused types, the stock is probably worth a deep dive. The market doesn't appear to be giving the manufacturer enough credit for its success on the development front, and that is probably tilting the risk-reward scale toward reward.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • From the start of 2026 to its peak on Oct.
    • Recent findings suggest that investors might be worried about a few things.
    • Even after its recent pullback, the S&P 500 index has risen 229% in 10 years.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Neil Patel – Nov 20, 2026 at 7:23PM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than S&P 500 Index ›.

    From the start of 2026 to its peak on Oct. 6, the S&P 500 index (^GSPC -3.70%), the measuring stick for how the U.S. equity market is performing, posted a price return of 14%. Since that all-time high, though, the benchmark has fallen about 10% (as of Nov. 19).

    Recent findings suggest that investors might be worried about a few things. They could be more skeptical about all the artificial intelligence (AI) data center spending that's taking place. Elevated inflation and rising interest rates are stealing the show from a macro perspective. And we're past a midterm election cycle that saw the Democrats take control of Congress, introducing regulatory uncertainty.

    Sources indicate that step back. Even after its recent pullback, the S&P 500 index has risen 229% in 10 years. Here's what a $1,000 investment made in the Vanguard S&P 500 ETF (VOO -3.42%) a decade ago could have become today.

    In a recent development, the S&P 500 index climbed at a 12.6% annualized rate over the past decade, before dividends. Including dividends, a $1,000 investment in the Vanguard S&P 500 ETF 10 years ago would be worth about $3,953 today. That's a 14.7% annualized total return. Investors almost quadrupled their money.

    The recent drop is a blip on the massive-picture radar. Even after sliding since early October, the index is still up slightly in 2026.

    Recent findings suggest that what powered the gains? It's mostly earnings. In December 2016, the S&P 500 traded at a forward price-to-earnings (P/E) ratio of 17. This compares the index's price to the profits analysts expect over the next 12 months. Today, the multiple is around 18, slightly below its 10-year average.

    Industry observers note that based on this metric, the valuation barely moved. Forward earnings per share, meanwhile, jumped from $133 (at the end of 2016) to $416 in early November of this year, a 212% increase. Investors didn't make money by paying higher prices. They built wealth because American businesses became far more profitable.

    According to recent reports, one sector stands above the rest. Information technology, measured by the Vanguard Information Technology ETF (VGT -7.00%) delivered an annualized total return of roughly 22.7% in the last decade. AI, cloud computing, and surrounding internet-based secular trends made trillion-dollar market caps a common theme. The tech sector now represents 37% of the S&P 500 index. VOO investors own those winners automatically, for an expense ratio of just 0.03%.

    NYSEMKT · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

    Those gains weren't easy to hold on to. The S&P 500 index fell nearly 20% in late 2018, crashed 34% during the COVID-19 panic, slid 25% in the 2022 bear market, and dropped 19% during the 2025 tariff scare. This year alone has brought two declines of 8% or more. Volatility is just a part of the game.

    Each time the market fell, selling felt like the right move. But each time, the index eventually bounced back and went on to latest highs.

    Industry observers note that investors who trade in and out usually pay for it. Morningstar's (MORN -0.30%) latest Mind the Gap study found that the average dollar in U.S. mutual funds and ETFs earned 8.7% per year over the decade ended 2025. The funds themselves returned 9.9%. The difference is due to poorly timed buying and selling.

    Missing a few days hurts, too. According to J.P. Morgan (JPM -3.03%) Asset Management, sitting out the 10 best days over the 20-year period from 2006 through 2025 would have cut an investor's annualized return from 11% to 6.6%, an enormous difference.

    Dollar-cost averaging is the solution. This means investing a set amount on a regular schedule, regardless of price. There's no guessing involved. Adding steadily in this manner to the Vanguard S&P 500 ETF is no doubt one of the simplest ways to build wealth.

    When the market is down, like it is now, hang in there.The best results of the past decade came from holding through every pullback.

    #39356. Industry News: Junk bonds are 'flashing yellow.' Watch these warning signs

    📅 09 Oct 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (1038 w)
    📖 Baca
    Gadgets ⚠️ Warning 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

    Industry News: Junk bonds are 'flashing yellow.' Watch these warning signs

    📅 09 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1038 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Cracks are forming in the junk bond market as investors demand higher payouts for owning the market's riskiest debt.
    • Sources indicate that high-yield bonds now yield 8.1%, up from 7.22% a month ago.
    • Sources indicate that the high-yield market is also showing stress on the credit side with spreads recently widening to levels not seen since April, according to the Federal Reserve Bank of St.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Cracks are forming in the junk bond market as investors demand higher payouts for owning the market's riskiest debt. It isn't time to ditch high-yield bonds, but investors should pay attention to the warning signs.

    Sources indicate that high-yield bonds now yield 8.1%, up from 7.22% a month ago. The increase reflects a jump in yields across the curve as investors bake in more inflation from high energy prices and other pressures, including concern about the deficit — hitting nearly $2 trillion in the fiscal year that ended Sept. 30.

    Sources indicate that the high-yield market is also showing stress on the credit side with spreads recently widening to levels not seen since April, according to the Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis. Credit spreads are the difference in yield between the bonds and Treasurys of similar maturities. Wider spreads mean investors are demanding higher yields for holding corporate debt, viewing it as riskier.

    Sources indicate that spreads are at 315 basis points in the overall high-yield market, higher than a year ago but still below levels in March when they reached 346 bps. One basis point equals one one-hundredth of a percent, or 0.01%.

    Recent findings suggest that the high-yield market consists of bonds rated BB+ by S&P and Fitch and Ba1 and under by Moody's. The lowest-rated cohort, CCC and below, has seen the most movement with spreads climbing dramatically over the past year to roughly 1,250 bps.

    Right now, the high-yield market is "flashing yellow" but is "far from red," said Michael Arone, chief investment strategist at State Street Investment Management.

    It makes sense that investors are demanding more compensation for taking on additional credit risk as borrowing costs rise, he said.

    Yields are elevated across the board with the 10-year Treasury reaching its highest level since 2002 earlier in the week.

    "The bigger question is whether this is simply a repricing of interest rate risk, or the beginning of a more fundamental reassessment of credit quality," Arone stated.

    He's in a wait-and-see mode since earnings are still growing, interest-coverage ratios remain good, and while default rates have ticked up some, he believes it is not concerning.

    That remarked, the starting point in spreads is likely weighing on investors' psyche, since they are still low by historical standards.

    In a recent development, "There's a small margin of error here, which I also think raises the anxiety level," Arone explained. "The compensation that investors are receiving for taking on this credit risk isn't overwhelming relative to history, and therefore subtle changes in credit spreads can be concerning.".

    While there may be concerns about part of the lower-rated market, the overall high-yield market is in good fundamental shape.

    In fact, credit quality is at a record high, with BB bonds making up over 60% of the market compared with 38% prior to the global financial crisis, said Kelley Gerrity, a fixed income strategist at Morgan Stanley Investment Management.

    According to recent reports, "We've had higher-quality companies coming in, and with higher rates now, you also have more discipline from companies that are more indebted ... just because of the higher cost of capital, so that actually is creating a bit of a healthier picture as well," she noted.

    Recent findings suggest that the lowest tier of high yield has always been more speculative, since the bonds have a higher default risk. Therefore, it's no surprise that they are the ones seeing the most widening in spreads, noted Collin Martin, head of fixed income research and strategy at the Schwab Center for Financial Research.

    The overall move in high-yield spreads have been "orderly," he said. "Are there cracks forming? I think the cracks are logical cracks with the lowest-rated bonds and it's too early to say that it's spreading to the broad credit market.".

    In a recent development, in addition, fluctuations within the CCC-rated and lower spreads have been idiosyncratic, Gerrity added. Morgan Stanley recently broke down the spreads in the lowest cohort into two buckets: performing assets and non-performing assets, which are defined as spreads above 1,000 bps.

    The non-performing spread to worst is 2,818 bps, while the performing bucket — the biggest piece of the CCC market — is 461 bps, she said.

    "It is isolated," she stated. "I'm not necessarily sure that that will go away anytime soon, but it doesn't tell the story of overall concern and flashing caution for credit markets right now.".

    For now, investors should remain selective within higher yield, Gerrity advised.

    "We're looking for the best relative value opportunities, and we think that exists within that single-B cohort, and so we're leaning into that," she said.

    Investors should be concerned if there is a steep widening in the broader high-yield market.

    In a recent development, but there's scant evidence of stress in the BB cohort. Spreads in that group are at 194 bps, up from 179 bps a year ago — although the move hasn't been in a straight line.

    "We're going to be focusing our attention on what are considered some stronger businesses," Martin said. "If we start to see the markets demand higher spreads there also, that's what we'll be looking at to see if risks are really rising.".

    Recent findings suggest that it's also crucial to understand that the Federal Reserve is raising rates in a strong economic environment, said R.J. Gallo, chief investment officer of global fixed income at Federated Hermes. The central bank is concerned about an inflation problem amid high fossil fuel prices due to the Iran war, while growth has been stronger than expected, he noted.

    "With growth being good as the reason that the Fed is hiking, then you wouldn't expect high yield to blow out because growth means revenues stay up, means cash flow and profitability stays up," he explained.

    High yield becomes a disaster when the economy is heading into a sharp economic downturn, Gallo said.

    Recent findings suggest that "That's when spreads really widen out," he said. "But a recession is not the odds-on bet. Now, talk to me in six months if the Fed keeps hiking over and over, if oil prices stay high for longer, well, then maybe we will start to wonder.".

Recent research from Goldman suggests that the benchmark S&P index will gain 26% in the next 12 months by November 2027, despite possibly lower earnings growth compared to 2026.Let's look at what this might mean for investors -- and why it's a good sign to keep buying stocks with low-cost index funds like S&P 500 ETFs.

    Goldman strategists predict that the S&P 500 will reach 8,700 points in the next 12 months. On Nov. 20, the index closed at about 6,910, so this would imply a gain of about 26% from that level.

    In a recent development, that's not an outlandish return to expect for the S&P 500. A 26% gain in 12 months would be an exceptionally strong year, much better than the average. But it's well within the realm of possibility.

    Recent findings suggest that keep in mind that the long-term average annual return for the S&P 500, based on historical data since 1928, is 9.98%. And in the past few years, the Vanguard S&P 500 ETF (VOO -3.42%) has delivered annual returns of about 17.8% in 2025, 25% in 2024, and 26.3% in 2023.

    NYSEMKT · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

    Why does Goldman think the S&P 500 will do so well in the next 12 months? If so many investors are nervous about tech companies spending too much on AI data centers, isn't now a bad time to buy the S&P? After all, as of Nov. 19, eight of the top 10 holdings in the S&P 500 were tech names, and those top eight stocks made up about 33.5% of the index by weight.

    The answer is in the valuations.

    Recent investor skepticism about AI stocks might actually be healthy for future returns. Recent declines in tech stock prices have driven down those companies' valuations. Goldman's research finds that AI hyperscalers are trading "well below" their historic valuations and says that "we see Technology -- and Hyperscalers in particular -- as relatively defensive.".

    The very same tech stocks that have been going through a correction in the past month might be poised for bigger gains in the next 12 months. Goldman notes that even though some of the biggest hyperscalers have negative cash flow due to their aggressive AI investments, these companies still have strong balance sheets and could become attractive in the next 12 months if growth opportunities elsewhere are harder to find.

    Recent findings suggest that this trend of lower valuations can also be seen if you look at the S&P 500 index forward price-to-earnings ratio (P/E). This metric demonstrates the index's earnings multiple based on the next 12 months' estimated earnings. The S&P forward P/E has dropped from a recent high of 30 to 21.08, trading at about a 15% discount compared to its five-year average.

    S&P 500 P/E Ratio Forward Estimate data by YCharts.

    Long-term investors need to think beyond today, tomorrow, or even the next 12 months. One year is not "long term." But this Goldman Sachs research is a helpful sign that there are many reasons to be optimistic about the stock market, despite some recent volatility.

    It has been revealed that if you share Goldman's optimism about the S&P 500 in 2027, now can be a good time to buy low-cost index funds like the Vanguard S&P 500 ETF (VOO). This ultra-low-cost ETF lets you track the performance of the S&P.

    It has been revealed that you don't have to pick stocks or worry about which companies or industries are winning or losing; this Vanguard ETF lets you own 500 of the largest publicly traded companies in America, representing about 80% of the total U.S. stock market. If Goldman's analysis is on target, your investment in the ETF could go up by 26% in the next 12 months.

    But even if that forecast doesn’t come true, you can rest assured that the S&P 500 has delivered strong average annual returns of about 10% for long-term investors who can buy and hold through temporary ups and downs along the way.

    When our analyst team has a stock tip, it can pay to listen. After all, Stock Advisor's total average return is 768%* — a market-crushing outperformance compared to 199% for the S&P 500.

    Latest Update: NFL news, live updates: Colts release Daniel Jones, Anthony Richardson Sr. to start at QB; Puka Nacua potentially out for season after knee surgery

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • We are officially halfway done with the 2026 NFL season, and the NFL is now into Week 11, highlighted by the year's final international game: the Minnesota Vikings take on the San Francisco 49ers in Mexico City, Mexico, for "Sunday Night Football.".
    • The Indianapolis Colts and Houston Texans opened up the week on "Thursday Night Football," but quarterback Daniel Jones continued to struggle, completing just 44.4% of pass attempts for 144 yards and a pick.
    • Sources indicate that los Angeles Rams receiver Puka Nacua might be done for the year after undergoing surgery on his MCL on Tuesday.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    We are officially halfway done with the 2026 NFL season, and the NFL is now into Week 11, highlighted by the year's final international game: the Minnesota Vikings take on the San Francisco 49ers in Mexico City, Mexico, for "Sunday Night Football.".

    The Indianapolis Colts and Houston Texans opened up the week on "Thursday Night Football," but quarterback Daniel Jones continued to struggle, completing just 44.4% of pass attempts for 144 yards and a pick. The Colts followed up with a statement move on Friday, announcing the team would release Jones and promote former No. 4 overall pick Anthony Richardson Sr. to the starting position in a stunning move.

    Sources indicate that los Angeles Rams receiver Puka Nacua might be done for the year after undergoing surgery on his MCL on Tuesday. Nacua was already on injured reserve with multiple injuries, but head coach Sean McVay says that he is now poised to miss "a couple months.".

    That news came one day after Nacua was reportedly suspended three games by the NFL for violating the league's personal conduct policy, as a result of the receiver's series of incidents this offseason; Nacua is serving the suspension while on IR.

    Follow along with Yahoo Sports for the latest NFL news, injury updates, and more.

    Patriots receiver A.J. Brown is poised to miss significant time: The wideout is expected to be sidelined for multiple weeks after suffering a hastring injury last week, per ESPN's Adam Schefter and Mike Reiss.

    Brown has played in just four games this season after sustaining several separate injuries. He was questionable heading into last Sunday's game with ankle and knee complications, but was able to play before suffering the hamstring injury.

    The Chiefs will likely be without Kenneth Walker III again for their Week 11 game against the Cardinals, head coach Andy Reid said Friday.

    According to recent reports, walker reported groin tightness last week, and the team decided to give him a rest and sit out the 35-13 win over the Atlanta Falcons. Reid said on Wednesday that the running back was "feeling better," but they did not "want to do something stupid.".

    Through 10 weeks, Walker is fourth in rushing in the NFL with 872 yards and tied for fifth in the league among running backs with seven touchdowns.

    Read more about Walker's injury here.

    Recent findings suggest that following testing, New England Patriots quarterback Drake Maye reportedly suffered a fractured right fibula in Week 10, per ESPN. Maye sustained the injury after taking a sack on the first drive of Sunday's 35-10 loss to the Lions.

    Maye will not require surgery and there is a small chance he could be back for the Patriots late in the regular season if they are contending for an AFC playoff spot.

    Read more about Maye's injury here.

    Industry observers note that in a stunning move, Indianapolis has released starting quarterback Daniel Jones. Head coach Shane Steichen announced the news on Friday, adding that Anthony Richardson will be the team's upcoming starting QB going forward.

    It has been revealed that after being limited in practice on Thursday, Cardinals quarterback Carson Beck will sit out Friday. Head coach Mike LaFleur said the team will prepare veteran Josh Johnson to start this week against the Chiefs.

    The 40-year-old Johnson made two starts last season with the Commanders. The Cardinals are his 15th NFL season.

    After sitting out practice earlier this week, Buccaneers quarterback Baker Mayfield is heading in the right direction to get back on the field on Sunday.

    Sources indicate that mayfield missed Wednesday's practice with injuries to his foot and right thumb, and was limited in practice on Thursday. Though Mayfield's designation for Friday isn't yet available, head coach Todd Bowles told reporters Friday that Mayfield looked good in practice and was trending in the right direction to start.

    Mayfield has been dealing with these injuries, but hasn't missed any time. Tampa Bay had a bye last weekend, giving their quarterback a bit more time to rest.

    The injury woes of Rams wide receiver Puka Nacua just got more severe: On Friday, head coach Sean McVay confirmed that Nacua had undergone surgery on his MCL on Tuesday, and that he'll be out for "a couple months." Timeline-wise, that might rule the receiver out for the rest of the season.

    It has been revealed that nacua was already on injured reserve with knee and turf toe injuries. He is also serving a three-game suspension for violating the league's personal conduct policy, with the suspension occurring while he's on IR.

    Smith left Sunday's game after injuring his ankle. The quarterback has been limited this this week in practice, but will be a full participant on Friday, head coach Aaron Glenn stated.

    Wide receivers Omar Cooper Jr. (ankle/hip) and Isaiah Williams (ribs) have been ruled out. DT David Onyemata (abdomen), who had his 21-day practice window opened this week, will remain out.

    As the 49ers practiced against the backdrop of the Rocky Mountains this week, the Vikings tried to bring Mexico City to the Midwest. They erected a massive altitude chamber at their Eagan practice facility that simulates the low-pressure environment found at elevations as high as 12,000 feet.

    Sources indicate that over the past five weeks, Vikings players have subjected themselves to aerobic workouts inside the chamber, using treadmills and stationary bikes to simulate the demands of exercising at altitude. The Vikings hope that altitude training inside their own building reduces the shock factor they experience Sunday night, Tyler Williams, the team's vice president of player health and performance, told reporters in Minnesota on Wednesday.

    In an Instagram post, the two-time Pro Bowl defensive end pledged to come back from his injury stronger than ever and to never again jump up to celebrate a major play.

    In a recent development, "I honestly can't believe it," Hutchinson wrote in his post. "I've jumped hundreds of times on a football field and never in a million years did I think this would happen to me. But even something like this won't hold me back.".

    It has been revealed that "Two things I know for sure," he added. "1. I always come back stronger. 2. That's the last time I go airborne.".

    Hutchinson injured his knee on the Lions' first defensive series during their matchup in Munich with the Latest England Patriots on Sunday.

    In a recent development, reed played 15 of his 16 NFL seasons in Buffalo and was part of those Bills teams that reached four straight Super Bowls. Over 234 career games, he made 951 receptions for 13,198 yards and 87 touchdowns.

    The two-time All-Pro and seven-time Pro Bowler was inducted into the Pro Football Hall of Fame in 2014.

    On Thursday, Richardson entered midway through the fourth quarter and missed his first two throws of the night. There was no second series; the Texans ran out the clock. And it almost feels like the Colts are trying to run out the clock on Richardson, Jones, Riley Leonard — all of it.

    In a recent development, head coach Shane Steichen this week said he takes "everything into account" when it comes to the quarterbacks. He added: "Obviously, the biggest thing is taking care of the football moving forward.".

    Asked about a potential QB change after Thursday's loss, Steichen remarked, "we'll evaluate everything.".

    Recent findings suggest that los Angeles Rams wide receiver Puka Nacua has been suspended for three games for violating the league's personal conduct policy, the NFL revealed Thursday. ESPN's Adam Schefter was the first to report it.

    It has been revealed that nacua's suspension will go into effect immediately, and he will be eligible for reinstatement on Monday, Dec. 14. The All-Pro wideout is right now on injured reserve with knee and turf toe injuries sustained in Week 9's win over the Washington Commanders, and head coach Sean McVay has stated he is expected to miss "significant time." If he were healthy by Dec. 14, he would not miss any additional time because of the suspension.

    It has been revealed that nacua's suspension comes following a roller coaster of an offseason, as he faced a civil lawsuit from a woman over an alleged biting incident and antisemitic comments earlier this year. An attorney representing Nacua denied the woman's claim that he made the antisemitic comment while downplaying the bite mark he left on her.

    The Bengals quarterback will not speak on his normal day as he is dealing with an illness, according to the team. If he's feeling better on Friday, he will meet with reporters. He did appear on the practice field and was seen throwing during the open portion, according to The Athletic's Paul Dehner Jr.

    According to recent reports, the 49ers got a welcome sight on Thursday with wide receiver Mike Evans taking part in practice for the first time in a month. The 33-year-old has not played since Week 6 as he deals with an Achilles injury. San Francisco takes on the Vikings on Sunday night in Week 11.

    Recent findings suggest that after sitting out Wednesday, the Raiders tight end was back on the field for Thursday's practice. Klint Kubiak said earlier this week that Bowers is considered day-to-day as he deals with an ankle injury suffered during their Week 10 loss to the Seahawks.

    Parker is remaining on as DC, but Mike Pettine will call plays on the defensive side of the ball.

    Sources indicate that "A different perspective [will be] good for us," head coach Brian Schottenheimer stated Wednesday. "Play-calling is a very collaborative thing.".

    On Thursday, Parker addressed the change saying it's "not ideal" and did not comment directly when asked about his future in Dallas.

    When asked about his future with the Cowboys, Parkers left more up in the air: "We'll cross that bridge when we come to it.".

    Industry observers note that over four seasons in Denver, Moss has 196 total tackles and 3 interceptions. This season, the 26-year-old has 27 total tackle, 8 pass deflections and 1 interception through eight games.

    Moss was the Broncos' third-round pick in the 2023 NFL Draft.

    The Ravens have sent Humphrey home from the team facility on Thursday in the fallout from a joke about the city of Baltimore earlier this week, and he will be inactive for Week 11.

    In a recent development, during a segment on his podcast, Humphrey was asked what Baltimore was best at making. He first mentioned "The Star Spangled Banner" and National Bohemian beer, but then uttered a disparaging line that many have understandably found offensive.

    "What is Baltimore best at making?" Humphrey pondered. "They're best at making criminals.".

    In a recent development, buccaneers QB Baker Mayfield dealing with a foot strain and a thumb concern, did not practice on Wednesday. If Mayfield can't go against the Lions on Sunday, Jalon Daniels will get the call again.

    Geno Smith suffered an ankle injury on Sunday. He was limited during Wednesday's practice and the Jets believe the quarterback can start against the Chargers in Week 11.

    Sources indicate that groin tightness caused Chiefs running back Kenneth Walker III to sit out Week 10. That allowed rookie Emmett Johnson to run wild against the Falcons. Walker sat out Wednesday's practice and looks unlikely to play against on Sunday. The team could be eyeing the Thanksgiving Day night game against the Bills for a return.

    It's a drastic shift from the confidence and excitement that surrounded the 34-year-old Parker coming out of training camp, when a highly vocal and schematically multiple group of defenders had Dallas brass wondering whether they could solve multi-year defensive woes.

    In a recent development, parker has not fixed the Cowboys' defense as the unit ranks third-worst in points allowed per game (28.2) and worst in yards (393.8). But consider that last season's Cowboys ranked worst in points allowed and third-worst in yards a year after the Cowboys ranked second worst in points allowed and bottom-five in yards.

    The problems predate Parker. The fix remains elusive.
